bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【晋紀二十】起著雍涒灘，盡上章淹茂，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 20] From Zhuoyong Zuitan through Shangzhang Yanmao; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 20] From Zhuoyong Zuitan through Shangzhang Yanmao—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，林邑寇九真，殺士民什八九。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Linyi raided Jiuzhen and killed eight or nine tenths of the officials and common people.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Linyi invaded Jiuzhen and slaughtered perhaps ninety percent of the population.

sentences.zh: 趙秦公韜有寵于趙王虎，欲立之，以太子宣長，猶豫未决。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Tao was favored by Zhao King Hu, who wished to install him as heir; because Crown Prince Xuan was the elder son, he hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tao of Qin had won the favor of Zhao King Shi Hu, who wanted to make him heir, but because the crown prince Xuan was older, Hu wavered and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 宣嘗忤旨，虎怒曰：「悔不立韜也！」

translations.literal: Xuan once offended Hu's wishes; Hu raged and said, "I regret not having installed Tao!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had once defied him, and Hu flew into a rage, crying, "I regret not making Tao my heir!"

sentences.zh: 韜由是益驕，造堂于太尉府，號曰宣光殿，梁長九丈。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tao grew all the more arrogant; he built a hall in the Grand Commandant's compound, called it the Hall of Proclaiming Brilliance, and its beams were nine zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Tao grew ever more arrogant. He built a hall in the Grand Commandant's residence, named it the Hall of Proclaiming Brilliance, and made its beams nine zhang in length.

sentences.zh: 宣見而大怒，斬匠，截梁而去；

translations.literal: When Xuan saw it he was greatly enraged; he executed the craftsmen and had the beams cut down and removed;
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan saw it he was furious. He had the craftsmen executed and the beams cut down and hauled away;

sentences.zh: 韜怒，增之至十丈。

translations.literal: Tao was enraged and had them extended to ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, furious in turn, had them lengthened to ten zhang.

sentences.zh: 宣聞之，謂所幸楊柸、牟成、趙生曰：「凶竪傲愎乃敢爾！

translations.literal: When Xuan heard of it he said to his favorites Yang Pei, Mou Cheng, and Zhao Sheng, "That vicious wretch is so arrogant and obstinate that he dares do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan heard of this he said to his favorites Yang Pei, Mou Cheng, and Zhao Sheng, "That vicious brute is so arrogant and headstrong that he dares go this far!

sentences.zh: 汝能殺之，吾入西宮，當盡以韜之國邑分封汝等。

translations.literal: If you can kill him, when I enter the Western Palace I shall divide and enfeoff you with all of Tao's fiefs and estates.
translations.idiomatic: If you kill him, once I take the Western Palace I will divide Tao's entire domain among you as your fiefs.

sentences.zh: 韜死，主上必臨喪，吾因行大事，蔑不濟矣。」

translations.literal: When Tao is dead the sovereign is sure to come in person to the mourning; I shall then carry out the great deed—nothing can fail."
translations.idiomatic: When Tao is dead the emperor will certainly come to the funeral in person. I will seize that moment to strike—and nothing can stop me."

sentences.zh: 柸等許諾。

translations.literal: Pei and the others promised.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，韜夜與僚屬宴于東明觀，因宿于佛精舍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Tao feasted at night with his staff at the Eastern Brightness Observatory and lodged afterward in a Buddhist monastery.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Tao gave a night banquet for his staff at the Eastern Brightness Observatory and stayed overnight in a Buddhist cloister.

sentences.zh: 宣使楊柸等緣獼猴梯而入，殺韜，置其刀箭而去。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Yang Pei and the others to climb in on a monkey ladder, kill Tao, and leave his swords and arrows behind.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Yang Pei and the others to scale the wall on a rope ladder, kill Tao, and leave his swords and arrows at the scene.

sentences.zh: 旦日，宣奏之，虎哀驚氣絕，久之方蘇。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Xuan reported it; Hu grieved and was so shocked that he stopped breathing, and only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xuan reported the murder. Hu was stricken with grief and shock until he lost consciousness, and only after a long while did he come to.

sentences.zh: 將出臨其喪，司空李農諫曰：「害秦公者未知何人，賊在京師，鑾輿不宜輕出。」

translations.literal: He was about to go out in person to the mourning when Minister of Works Li Nong remonstrated, saying, "Who killed the Prince of Qin is still unknown; the assassin is in the capital, and the imperial carriage ought not go forth lightly."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to attend the funeral in person, Minister of Works Li Nong urged him: "We still do not know who killed the Prince of Qin. The killer is in the capital—the imperial carriage must not venture out lightly."

sentences.zh: 虎乃止，嚴兵發哀于太武殿。

translations.literal: Hu then stopped, arrayed troops, and held the mourning rites at the Hall of Grand Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: Hu desisted, deployed troops, and conducted the mourning rites at the Hall of Grand Martiality.

sentences.zh: 宣往臨韜喪，不哭，直言「呵呵」，使舉衾觀尸，大笑而去。

translations.literal: Xuan went to Tao's mourning, did not weep, and only said "Heh heh"; he had the covering lifted to view the corpse, laughed loudly, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan went to Tao's funeral, shed no tears, and only muttered "Heh, heh." He had the shroud raised to look at the corpse, laughed aloud, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 收大將軍記室參軍鄭靖、尹武等，將委之以罪。

translations.literal: He arrested the Grand General's secretariat aides Zheng Jing, Yin Wu, and others, intending to lay the crime on them.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Grand General's secretariat aides Zheng Jing and Yin Wu, among others, intending to blame them for the murder.

sentences.zh: 虎疑宣殺韜，欲召之，恐其不入，乃詐言其母杜-{后}-哀過危惙；

translations.literal: Hu suspected that Xuan had killed Tao and wished to summon him but feared he would not come; he therefore falsely reported that Xuan's mother, Empress Du, was gravely ill from excessive mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Hu suspected Xuan of the murder and wanted to summon him but feared he would refuse. He therefore spread a false report that Xuan's mother, Empress Du, was critically ill with grief;

sentences.zh: 宣不謂見疑，入朝中宮，因留之。

translations.literal: Xuan, not thinking himself suspected, entered the palace to the inner quarters and was detained there.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, unaware that he was suspected, entered the inner palace—and was held there.

sentences.zh: 建興人史科知其謀，告之；

translations.literal: Shi Ke of Jianxing knew of the plot and reported it;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke of Jianxing learned of the plot and informed the court;

sentences.zh: 虎使收楊柸、牟成，皆亡去；

translations.literal: Hu sent to arrest Yang Pei and Mou Cheng, but both fled;
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent men to arrest Yang Pei and Mou Cheng, but both escaped;

sentences.zh: 獲趙生，詰之，具服。

translations.literal: Zhao Sheng was captured, interrogated, and confessed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Sheng was seized, questioned, and confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 虎悲怒彌甚，囚宣于席庫，以鐵環穿其頷而鏁之，取殺韜刀箭，舐其血，哀號震動宮殿。

translations.literal: Hu's grief and rage grew all the greater; he imprisoned Xuan in the storehouse, pierced his jaw with an iron ring and locked it, took the sword and arrows that had killed Tao, licked their blood, and wailed so that the palace halls shook.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's grief and fury only deepened. He imprisoned Xuan in a storeroom, ran an iron ring through his jaw and locked it, took the sword and arrows that had killed Tao, licked the blood from them, and wailed until the palace halls rang.

sentences.zh: 佛圖澄曰：「宣、起皆陛下之子，今爲韜殺宣，是重禍也。

translations.literal: Fotudeng said, "Xuan and Qi were both Your Majesty's sons; now, because of Tao, to kill Xuan is to heap calamity upon calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Fotudeng said, "Xuan and Qi were both your sons. To kill Xuan now for Tao's sake is to pile misfortune upon misfortune.

sentences.zh: 陛下若加慈恕，福祚猶長。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty shows mercy and forbearance, your blessings may yet be prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: If you show mercy, your fortune may yet endure.

sentences.zh: 若必誅之，宣當爲彗星下掃鄴宮。」

translations.literal: If you insist on executing him, Xuan will become a comet descending to sweep clean the palace at Ye."
translations.idiomatic: If you must put him to death, Xuan will become a comet that sweeps Ye clean."

sentences.zh: 虎不從。

translations.literal: Hu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 積柴于鄴北，樹標其上，標末置鹿盧，穿之以繩，倚梯柴積。

translations.literal: He piled firewood north of Ye, set a pole atop it, fixed a pulley at the pole's tip, threaded a rope through it, and leaned a ladder against the pyre.
translations.idiomatic: He heaped firewood north of Ye, erected a pole on the pile, fitted a pulley at its top, ran a rope through it, and set a ladder against the stack.

sentences.zh: 送宣其下，使韜所幸宦者郝稚、劉霸拔其髪，抽其舌，牽之登梯。

translations.literal: Xuan was brought below; the eunuchs Hao Zhi and Liu Ba, whom Tao had favored, were made to pull out his hair, draw out his tongue, and drag him up the ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was brought to the pyre. The eunuchs Hao Zhi and Liu Ba, whom Tao had favored, were ordered to tear out his hair, pull out his tongue, and haul him up the ladder.

sentences.zh: 郝稚以繩貫其頷，鹿盧絞上。

translations.literal: Hao Zhi ran the rope through Xuan's jaw and hoisted him with the pulley.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhi threaded the rope through Xuan's jaw and hauled him up on the pulley.

sentences.zh: 劉霸斷其手足，斫眼潰腸，如韜之傷。

translations.literal: Liu Ba severed his hands and feet, gouged out his eyes and burst his bowels, matching Tao's wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba cut off his hands and feet, gouged out his eyes, and ripped open his belly—mirroring Tao's injuries.

sentences.zh: 四面縱火，烟炎際天，虎從昭儀已下數千人登中臺以觀之。

translations.literal: Fire was set on all sides; smoke and flames reached the sky. Hu, with several thousand people from the ladies of the harem downward, mounted the central terrace to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Fire was lit on every side until smoke and flame filled the sky. Hu, accompanied by several thousand women of the harem and below, climbed the central terrace to watch.

sentences.zh: 火滅，取灰分置諸門交道中。

translations.literal: When the fire died out, the ashes were gathered and scattered at the crossroads before every gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the fire burned out, the ashes were collected and strewn at the crossroads before every gate.

sentences.zh: 殺其妻子九人。

translations.literal: Nine of his wives and children were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Nine of his wives and children were executed.

sentences.zh: 宣小子才數歲，虎素愛之，抱之而泣，欲赦之，其大臣不聽，就抱中取而殺之。

translations.literal: Xuan's young son was only a few years old; Hu had always loved him, held him weeping, and wished to spare him, but his ministers would not agree and took the child from his arms to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's little boy was only a few years old. Hu had always doted on him, held him in his arms weeping, and wanted to spare him, but his ministers would not permit it and snatched the child from his embrace to kill him.

sentences.zh: 兒挽虎衣大叫，至于絕帶，虎因此發病。

translations.literal: The boy clutched Hu's robe and screamed until the sash broke; because of this Hu fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The boy clutched Hu's robe and shrieked until the sash tore free—and Hu fell ill from the shock.

sentences.zh: 又廢其-{后}-杜氏爲庶人，誅其四率已下三百人，宦者五十人，皆車裂節解，弃之漳水。

translations.literal: He also deposed Empress Du to commoner status, executed three hundred men from the rank of colonel of four subordinates downward, and fifty eunuchs—all dismembered by chariot-tearing and joint-severing and cast into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Empress Du to commoner status, executed three hundred men from the rank of colonel downward, and fifty eunuchs—all torn apart by chariot and limb, then thrown into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 洿其東宮以養猪牛。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace was defiled and used to raise pigs and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was defiled and turned into a pig and cattle pen.

sentences.zh: 東官衛士十餘萬人皆謫戍凉州。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand guards of the Eastern Palace were banished to garrison duty in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand guards of the Eastern Palace were banished to frontier service in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，散騎常侍趙攬言于虎曰：「宮中將有變，宜備之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Regular Attendant Zhao Lan had said to Hu, "There will soon be trouble within the palace; you should take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Regular Attendant Zhao Lan had warned Hu, "There will soon be trouble in the palace—you should be on guard."

sentences.zh: 及宣殺韜，虎疑其知而不告，亦誅之。

translations.literal: When Xuan killed Tao, Hu suspected that Zhao had known but not reported it and executed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan killed Tao, Hu suspected Zhao had known but kept silent—and had him executed too.

sentences.zh: 朝廷論平蜀之功，欲以豫章郡封桓溫。

translations.literal: The court discussed rewards for pacifying Shu and wished to enfeoff Huan Wen with Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated how to reward Huan Wen for conquering Shu and proposed enfeoffing him with Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞荀蕤曰：「溫若復平河、洛，將何以賞之？」

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Rui said, "If Wen should later pacify the Yellow River and Luoyang regions, how will he be rewarded?"
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Rui said, "If Wen goes on to recover the Yellow River basin and Luoyang, what reward will be left for him?"

sentences.zh: 乃加溫征西大將軍、開府儀同三司，封臨賀郡公；

translations.literal: Thereupon Wen was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the West with authority equal to the Three Dukes and enfeoffed as Duke of Linhe commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Instead Wen was made Grand General Who Conquers the West, granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Dukes, and enfeoffed as Duke of Linhe;

sentences.zh: 加譙王無忌前將軍；

translations.literal: Prince of Qiao Wuji was made General of the Vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuji of Qiao was made General of the Vanguard;

sentences.zh: 袁喬龍驤將軍，封湘西伯。

translations.literal: Yuan Qiao was made General of the Flying Dragon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiao was made General of the Flying Dragon and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi.

sentences.zh: 蕤，崧之子也。

translations.literal: Rui was the son of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was the son of Xun Song.

sentences.zh: 溫既滅蜀，威名大振，朝廷憚之。

translations.literal: Once Wen had destroyed Shu, his martial renown shook the realm and the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen destroyed Shu his fame and power soared, and the court grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱以揚州刺史殷浩有盛名，朝野推服，乃引爲心膂，與參綜朝權，欲以抗溫，由是與溫寢相疑貳。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Yu, because Governor of Yangzhou Yin Hao enjoyed great fame and was admired by court and populace alike, drew him close as a trusted confidant and shared in governing the court, intending to counterbalance Wen; from this Wen and Yu grew ever more mutually suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Kuaiji, seeing that Yin Hao, governor of Yangzhou, enjoyed great renown and the trust of court and country, brought him in as a close adviser and shared power with him to counter Huan Wen—and from that day Wen and the prince grew steadily more suspicious of each other.

sentences.zh: 浩以征北長史荀羨、前江州刺史王羲之夙有令名，擢羨爲吳國內史，羲之爲護軍將軍，以爲羽翼。

translations.literal: Hao, because Chief Clerk of the North Campaign Xun Xian and former Governor of Jiangzhou Wang Xizhi had long enjoyed fine reputations, promoted Xian to Administrator of Wu and Xizhi to General Who Protects the Army, taking them as his wings.
translations.idiomatic: Hao promoted Xun Xian, chief clerk of the north campaign, to administrator of Wu, and Wang Xizhi, former governor of Jiangzhou, to General Who Protects the Army—both men of long-standing reputation whom he meant as his wings.

sentences.zh: 羨，蕤之弟；

translations.literal: Xian was Rui's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Xian was the younger brother of Rui;

sentences.zh: 羲之，導之從子也。

translations.literal: Xizhi was a nephew of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi was a nephew of Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 羲之以爲內外協和，然後國家可安，勸浩及羨不宜與溫構隙，浩不從。

translations.literal: Xizhi held that only when inner and outer circles were in harmony could the state be secure; he urged Hao and Xian not to pick a quarrel with Wen, but Hao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhi believed the state could be secure only when court and commanders worked in harmony, and urged Hao and Xian not to feud with Wen—but Hao refused.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝有疾，召世子俊屬之曰：「今中原未平，方資賢杰以經世務。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Huang fell ill and summoned the heir apparent Jun, entrusting him with the words, "The Central Plains are not yet pacified; we must rely on worthy men to govern the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huang of Yan fell ill and summoned his heir Jun. "The Central Plains are not yet recovered," he said. "We must rely on able men to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 恪智勇兼濟，才堪任重，汝其委之，以成吾志！」

translations.literal: Ke combines wisdom and courage; his talent can bear heavy responsibility—entrust affairs to him and fulfill my will!"
translations.idiomatic: Ke has both wisdom and courage, and talent enough for the heaviest burdens. Entrust him with power and fulfill my design!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陽士秋士行高潔，忠幹貞固，可托大事，汝善待之！」

translations.literal: He also said, "Yang Shiqiu is lofty in conduct, loyal, capable, and steadfast—great affairs may be entrusted to him; treat him well!"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Yang Shiqiu is upright, loyal, and steadfast—great affairs may be entrusted to him. Treat him well!"

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day bingshen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day bingshen, he died.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎議立太子，太尉張舉曰：「燕公斌有武略，彭城公遵有文德，惟陛下所擇。」

translations.literal: Zhao King Hu deliberated on installing an heir; Grand Commandant Zhang Ju said, "Prince of Yan Bin has martial strategy; Prince of Pengcheng Zun has civil virtue—let Your Majesty choose."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao King Hu debated whom to name heir. Grand Commandant Zhang Ju said, "Prince Bin of Yan has military talent; Prince Zun of Pengcheng has civil virtue—the choice is yours, Majesty."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「卿言正起吾意。」

translations.literal: Hu said, "Your words have just stirred my mind."
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "That is exactly what I had in mind."

sentences.zh: 戎昭將軍張豺曰：「燕公母賤，又嘗有過；

translations.literal: General Who Manifests Martial Prowess Zhang Chai said, "The Prince of Yan's mother was low-born, and he himself once committed an offense;
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Chai said, "Prince Bin's mother was of humble birth, and he himself once offended you;

sentences.zh: 彭城公母前以太子事廢，今立之，臣恐不能無微恨。

translations.literal: the Prince of Pengcheng's mother was earlier deposed over the matter of the crown prince; if he is installed now, I fear he cannot be without some lingering resentment.
translations.idiomatic: and Prince Zun's mother was deposed over the matter of the crown prince. If you name him heir now, I fear he may harbor some lingering resentment.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜審思之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should weigh this carefully."

sentences.zh: 初，虎之拔上邽也，張豺獲前趙主曜幼女安定公主，有殊色，納于虎，虎嬖之，生齊公世。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hu captured Shanggui, Zhang Chai obtained the former Zhao ruler Liu Yao's young daughter, Princess Anding, who was of extraordinary beauty; he presented her to Hu, who favored her, and she bore Prince of Qi Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hu took Shanggui, Zhang Chai captured the former Zhao ruler Liu Yao's young daughter, Princess Anding, a woman of rare beauty. He presented her to Hu, who doted on her, and she bore Prince Shi of Qi.

sentences.zh: 豺以虎老病，欲立世爲嗣，冀劉氏爲太后，己得輔政，乃說虎曰：「陛下再立太子，其母皆出于倡賤，故禍亂相尋；

translations.literal: Chai, because Hu was old and ill, wished to install Shi as heir, hoping that with the Liu clan as empress dowager he himself could govern; he therefore urged Hu, saying, "Your Majesty has twice installed crown princes whose mothers all came from singing-girls and the lowborn—hence calamities and rebellions have followed one after another;
translations.idiomatic: Chai, seeing Hu old and ill, wanted Shi named heir so that with the Liu clan as empress dowager he could rule behind the throne. He urged Hu: "Each time you have named an heir, the mother has been a singer or a woman of low birth—and each time disaster has followed;

sentences.zh: 今宜擇母貴子孝者立之。」

translations.literal: now you should choose one whose mother is noble and whose son is filial."
translations.idiomatic: you should choose a son whose mother is noble and who is himself filial."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「卿勿言，吾知太子處矣。」

translations.literal: Hu said, "Say no more—I know where the heir stands."
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Say no more. I know whom to name."

sentences.zh: 虎再與群臣議于東堂。

translations.literal: Hu again deliberated with his ministers in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hu again debated the matter with his ministers in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「吾欲以純灰三斛自滌其腸，何爲專生惡子，年逾二十輒欲殺父！

translations.literal: Hu said, "I wish to wash my bowels with three hu of pure ash—why do I keep bearing wicked sons who, once past twenty, want to kill their father!
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "I ought to scour my bowels with three hu of pure ash—why do I keep siring sons who, once they pass twenty, try to kill their father!

sentences.zh: 今世方十歲，比其二十，吾已老矣。」

translations.literal: This boy is only ten; by the time he is twenty, I shall already be old."
translations.idiomatic: This boy is only ten. By the time he is twenty, I will be an old man."

sentences.zh: 乃與張舉、李農定議，令公卿上書請立世爲太子。

translations.literal: He then settled the matter with Zhang Ju and Li Nong and ordered the high ministers to submit memorials requesting that Shi be installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He settled the matter with Zhang Ju and Li Nong and ordered the high ministers to memorialize asking that Shi be named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大司農曹莫不肯署名，虎使張豺問其故，莫頓首曰：「天下重器，不宜立少，故不敢署。」

translations.literal: Minister of Grand Granaries Cao Mo refused to sign; Hu sent Zhang Chai to ask why. Mo prostrated himself and said, "The great vessel of the realm ought not be given to the young; therefore I dare not sign."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Grand Granaries Cao Mo refused to sign. Hu sent Zhang Chai to ask why. Mo kowtowed and said, "The throne is the greatest trust of the realm—it should not go to a child. That is why I dare not sign."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「莫，忠臣也，然未達朕意；

translations.literal: Hu said, "Mo is a loyal minister, yet he has not grasped my intent;
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Mo is loyal, but he does not understand my mind;

sentences.zh: 張舉、李農知朕意矣，可令諭之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Ju and Li Nong understand my intent—have them explain it to him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju and Li Nong understand—have them explain it to him."

sentences.zh: 遂立世爲太子，以劉昭儀爲-{后}-。

translations.literal: Shi was thereupon installed as crown prince, and Lady Liu of the Bright Hall was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was named crown prince, and Lady Liu of the Bright Hall was made empress.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲辰，葬燕文明王。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on day jiachen, the Cultured King of Yan was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, on the day jiachen, the Cultured King of Yan was buried.

sentences.zh: 世子俊即位，赦境內，遣使詣建康告喪。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Jun succeeded to the throne, pardoned the realm, and sent envoys to Jiankang to announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Jun succeeded to the throne, proclaimed an amnesty within the realm, and sent envoys to Jiankang to announce the death.

sentences.zh: 以弟交爲左賢王，左長史陽騖郎中令。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiao was made Left Worthy King; the Left Chief Clerk Yang Xu was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jiao was made Left Worthy King, and the Left Chief Clerk Yang Xu was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以左光祿大夫、領司徒、錄尚書事蔡謨爲侍中、司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness Cai Mo, who also held the posts of Minister over the Masses and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Palace Attendant and Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Cai Mo, Left Grandee of Splendid Happiness, who also served as Minister over the Masses and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, was made Palace Attendant and Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 謨上疏固讓，謂所親曰：「我若爲司徒，將爲後代所曬，義不敢拜也。」

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial firmly declining, and said to those close to him, "If I become Minister over the Masses, later generations will mock me; by right I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: Mo memorialized firmly to decline, telling those close to him, "If I accept the post of Minister over the Masses, posterity will laugh at me—and by honor I dare not accept."

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of day xinwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, the day xinwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎即皇帝位，大赦，改元太寧，諸子皆進爵爲王。

translations.literal: Zhao King Hu assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Taining, and advanced all his sons to the rank of king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao King Shi Hu took the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Taining, and promoted all his sons to kings.

sentences.zh: 故東宮高力等萬餘人謫戍凉州，行達雍城，既不在赦例，又敕雍州剌史張茂送之，茂皆奪其馬，使之步推鹿車，致糧戍所。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand former Eastern Palace "strong men" and the like were banished to garrison Liangzhou; when they reached Yongcheng they were excluded from the amnesty, and an edict ordered Governor of Yongzhou Zhang Mao to escort them on; Mao seized all their horses and made them walk, pushing deer carts to deliver grain to the garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand former Eastern Palace guards—the "strong men"—were banished to Liangzhou. At Yongcheng they learned they were excluded from the amnesty, and the emperor ordered Governor Zhang Mao of Yongzhou to see them on. Mao seized their horses and forced them to march on foot, pushing grain carts to the frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 高力督定陽梁犢因衆心之怨，謀作亂東歸，衆聞之，皆踴抃大呼。

translations.literal: The strong men's overseer Liang Du of Dingyang, taking advantage of the men's resentment, plotted rebellion and a return east; when the host heard of it, all leaped and stamped and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: Their overseer Liang Du of Dingyang, sensing the men's fury, plotted to rebel and march east. When the troops heard of it, they leaped and shouted with joy.

sentences.zh: 犢乃自稱晋征東大將軍，帥衆攻拔下辨；

translations.literal: Du then styled himself Jin Grand General Who Conquers the East and led the host to attack and capture Xiabian;
translations.idiomatic: Du styled himself Jin Grand General Who Conquers the East and led his men to capture Xiabian;

sentences.zh: 安西將軍劉寧自安定擊之，爲犢所敗。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Liu Ning attacked him from Anding and was defeated by Du.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the West Liu Ning marched from Anding to attack him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 高力皆多力善射，一當十餘人，雖無兵甲，掠民斧，施一丈柯，攻戰若神，所向崩潰；

translations.literal: The strong men were all powerful and skilled archers, each a match for more than ten men; though they lacked armor and weapons, they seized peasants' axes, fitted handles a zhang long, and fought like spirits—wherever they went, defenses collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: The strong men were powerful archers, each worth more than ten ordinary soldiers. Though they had no armor or proper weapons, they seized farmers' axes, fitted ten-foot handles, and fought like demons—wherever they struck, defenses crumbled;

sentences.zh: 戍卒皆隨之，攻陷郡縣，殺長吏、二千石，長驅而東，比至長安，衆已十萬。

translations.literal: garrison soldiers all followed them; they stormed commanderies and counties, killed chief officials and those of two-thousand-dan rank, and drove east at speed—by the time they reached Chang'an their host already numbered a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: garrison troops joined them everywhere. They overran commanderies and counties, killed local officials, and swept east. By the time they reached Chang'an their force numbered a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 樂平王苞盡銳拒之，一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping Bao opposed them with his best troops and was defeated in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bao of Leping met them with his best troops and was routed in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 犢遂東出潼關，進趣洛陽。

translations.literal: Du then marched east out of Tong Pass and pressed toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Du marched east through Tong Pass and pressed toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 趙主虎以李農爲大都督、行大將軍事，統衛軍將軍張賀度等步騎十萬討之，戰于新安，農等大敗；

translations.literal: Zhao ruler Hu made Li Nong Grand Commander and acting Grand General, commanding Palace Guard General Zhang Hedu's infantry and cavalry of a hundred thousand to suppress them; they fought at Xin'an and Nong's forces were utterly defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao ruler Hu appointed Li Nong Grand Commander and acting Grand General, with a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry under Palace Guard General Zhang Hedu to crush the rebels. They met at Xin'an and Li Nong was routed;

sentences.zh: 戰于洛陽，又敗，退壁成皋。

translations.literal: they fought again at Luoyang and were defeated again, retreating to fortify Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: they fought again at Luoyang, were beaten again, and fell back to fortify Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 犢遂東掠滎陽、陳留諸郡，虎大懼，以燕王斌爲大都督，督中外諸軍事，統冠軍大將軍姚弋仲、車騎將軍蒲洪等討之。

translations.literal: Du then raided east through the commanderies of Xingyang, Chenliu, and others; Hu was greatly afraid and made Prince of Yan Bin Grand Commander, superintendent of all military affairs within and without, to command Champion General Yao Yizhong, General of Chariots and Cavalry Pu Hong, and others against him.
translations.idiomatic: Du swept east through Xingyang, Chenliu, and neighboring commanderies. Hu was terrified and named Prince Bin of Yan Grand Commander, superintendent of all armies at court and in the field, with Champion General Yao Yizhong, General of Chariots and Cavalry Pu Hong, and others to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 弋仲將其衆八千餘人至鄴，求見虎。

translations.literal: Yizhong led his host of more than eight thousand to Ye and requested an audience with Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong led more than eight thousand men to Ye and asked to see Hu.

sentences.zh: 虎病，未之見，引入領軍省，賜以己所御食。

translations.literal: Hu was ill and did not see him; he was brought into the Directorate of the Guards and given food from Hu's own table.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was ill and would not receive him. Yizhong was led into the Directorate of the Guards and offered food from the emperor's own table.

sentences.zh: 弋仲怒，不食，曰：「主上召我來擊賊，當面見授方略，我豈爲食來邪！

translations.literal: Yizhong was enraged and would not eat, saying, "The sovereign summoned me to strike the rebels and should meet me face to face to hand down strategy—did I come for a meal!
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong was furious and refused to eat. "The emperor summoned me to fight rebels," he said. "He should meet me in person and give me my orders—did I come for a meal?

sentences.zh: 且主上不見我，我何以知其存亡邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the sovereign will not see me, how am I to know whether he is alive or dead!"
translations.idiomatic: And if he will not see me, how am I to know whether he is alive or dead?"

sentences.zh: 虎力疾見之，弋仲讓虎曰：「兒死，愁邪？

translations.literal: Hu forced himself, ill as he was, to see him. Yizhong reproached Hu, saying, "Your son is dead—are you grieving?
translations.idiomatic: Hu dragged himself from his sickbed to see him. Yizhong rebuked him: "Your son is dead—are you grieving?

sentences.zh: 何爲而病？

translations.literal: Why then are you ill?
translations.idiomatic: Then why lie sick in bed?

sentences.zh: 兒幼時不擇善人教之，使至于爲逆；

translations.literal: When the boy was young you did not choose good men to teach him, until he came to act rebelliously;
translations.idiomatic: When he was a child you failed to choose worthy teachers, and so he grew into rebellion;

sentences.zh: 既爲逆而誅之，又何愁焉！

translations.literal: Once he had turned rebellious and you put him to death, what further grief is there!
translations.idiomatic: Once he rebelled and you executed him, what is there left to grieve?

sentences.zh: 且汝久病，所立兒幼，汝若不愈，天下必亂。

translations.literal: Moreover you have been ill a long time, and the son you have installed is young; if you do not recover, the realm will surely fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: You have been ill for years, and the heir you have named is still a child. If you do not recover, the empire will surely collapse into chaos.

sentences.zh: 當先憂此，勿憂賊也！

translations.literal: You ought first to worry about this; do not worry about rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Worry about that first—not about bandits!

sentences.zh: 犢等窮困思歸，相聚爲盜，所過殘暴，何所能至！

translations.literal: Du and the rest are destitute and desperate to return home; they have gathered as robbers, and wherever they pass they commit atrocities—how far can they reach!
translations.idiomatic: Du and his men are cornered and longing to go home. They band together as brigands and ravage whatever lies in their path—how far can they possibly get?

sentences.zh: 老羌爲汝一舉了之！」

translations.literal: This old Qiang will settle it for you in one stroke!"
translations.idiomatic: Let this old Qiang finish them for you in a single stroke!"

sentences.zh: 弋仲情狷直，人無貴賤皆「汝」之，虎亦不之責，于坐授使持節、侍中、征西大將軍賜以鎧馬。

translations.literal: Yizhong's disposition was blunt and upright; to men high and low alike he said "you," and Hu did not blame him for it. Where he sat Hu invested him on the spot with the staff of office, Palace Attendant, and Grand General Who Conquers the West, and granted him armor and a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong was blunt and unyielding; he addressed everyone, high or low, as "you," and Hu never took offense. Still in his presence Hu invested him with the staff of office as Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Conquers the West, and gave him armor and a horse.

sentences.zh: 弋仲曰：「汝看老羌堪破賊否？」

translations.literal: Yizhong said, "Do you see whether this old Qiang can break the rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong asked, "Well—do you think this old Qiang can break the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 乃被鎧跨馬于庭中，因策馬南馳，不辭而出。

translations.literal: Then he donned armor, mounted a horse in the courtyard, spurred south at a gallop, and departed without farewell.
translations.idiomatic: He strapped on his armor, mounted in the courtyard, and galloped south without so much as a farewell.

sentences.zh: 遂與斌等擊犢于滎陽，大破之，斬犢首而還，討其餘黨，盡滅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Bin and the rest he struck Du at Xingyang, routed him utterly, beheaded Du and returned, pursued the remnant band, and extinguished them to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Bin and the others, smashed Du at Xingyang, took his head, and returned; then he hunted down the survivors and wiped them out entirely.

sentences.zh: 虎命弋仲劍履上殿，入朝不趨，進封西平郡公；

translations.literal: Hu ordered Yizhong to wear sword and shoes in the palace hall, to enter court without hastening his step, and advanced him to Duke of Xiping;
translations.idiomatic: Hu granted Yizhong the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the throne hall and entering court without quickening his step, and promoted him to Duke of Xiping;

sentences.zh: 蒲洪爲侍中、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、都督雍、秦州諸軍事、雍州剌史，進封略陽郡公。

translations.literal: Pu Hong was made Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, commander of all military affairs in Yong and Qin provinces, Governor of Yong, and advanced to Duke of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Hong became Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, commander of all armies in Yong and Qin, Governor of Yong, and Duke of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 始平人爲勖聚兵自稱將軍，趙樂平王苞討滅之，誅三千餘家。

translations.literal: A man of Shiping named Wei gathered troops and styled himself general; Zhao's Prince of Leping Bao marched against him and destroyed him, executing more than three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Shiping a man named Wei raised troops and proclaimed himself general. Prince Bao of Leping crushed the uprising and put more than three thousand households to the sword.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，益州刺史周撫、龍驤將軍朱燾出范賁，斬之，益州平。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Inspector of Yizhou Zhou Fu and Dragon Cavalry General Zhu Tao marched out of Fan Ben and beheaded him; Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Zhou Fu, inspector of Yizhou, and Zhu Tao, Dragon Cavalry General, advanced from Fan Ben, beheaded the rebel leader, and pacified the province.

sentences.zh: 詔遣謁者陳沈如燕，拜慕容俊爲使持節、侍中、大都督、督河北諸軍事、幽、平二州牧、大將軍、大單于、燕王。

translations.literal: An edict sent Envoy Chen Shen to Yan to invest Murong Jun with the staff of office as Palace Attendant, Grand Commander, commander of all military affairs north of the Yellow River, Governor of You and Ping, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Envoy Chen Shen to Yan to invest Murong Jun as Palace Attendant, Grand Commander, commander of all armies north of the Yellow River, Governor of You and Ping, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 桓溫遣督護滕畯帥交、廣之兵擊林邑王文于盧容，爲文所敗，退屯九真。

translations.literal: Huan Wen sent Protector-in-chief Teng Jun leading troops of Jiao and Guang to attack Wang Wen of Linyi at Lu Rong; Wen defeated them, and they withdrew to garrison Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen dispatched Teng Jun, Protector-in-chief, with troops from Jiao and Guang to attack Wang Wen of Linyi at Lu Rong. Wen routed them, and they fell back to Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，趙王虎病甚，以彭城王遵爲大將軍，鎮關右；

translations.literal: On day yimao, Zhao King Hu was gravely ill; he made Prince of Pengcheng Zun Grand General to guard the west;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Zhao King Shi Hu lay gravely ill. He named Prince Zun of Pengcheng Grand General to hold the western frontier;

sentences.zh: 燕王斌爲丞相，錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Bin Chancellor, Director of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bin of Yan Chancellor and Director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 張豺爲鎮衛大將軍、領軍將軍、吏部尚書；

translations.literal: Zhang Chai General Who Guards the Guard, General of the Palace Army, Minister of Personnel;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai General Who Guards the Guard, General of the Palace Army, and Minister of Personnel;

sentences.zh: 幷受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: all three to receive the testamentary edict and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: all three to receive the deathbed edict and serve as regents.

sentences.zh: 劉-{后}-惡斌輔政，恐不利于太子，與張豺謀去之。

translations.literal: Empress Liu hated Bin's holding power in government and feared it would not benefit the crown prince; with Zhang Chai she plotted to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu resented Bin's role as regent, fearing it would harm the crown prince, and conspired with Zhang Chai to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 斌時在襄國，遣使詐謂斌曰：「主上疾已漸翕，王須獵者，可小停也。」

translations.literal: Bin was then at Xiangguo; they sent an agent with a false message saying to Bin, "The sovereign's illness has already grown somewhat better, my lord—you who love the hunt may pause a little."
translations.idiomatic: Bin was then at Xiangguo. They sent a forged message: "His Majesty's condition has improved somewhat. Your Highness, devoted as you are to the chase, might pause your hunting for a time."

sentences.zh: 斌素好獵，嗜酒，遂留獵，且縱酒。

translations.literal: Bin had always loved hunting and wine; he therefore remained hunting and moreover indulged in drink.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had always been devoted to hunting and wine. He stayed in the field and drank freely.

sentences.zh: 劉氏與豺因矯詔稱斌無忠教之心，免官歸第，使豺弟雄帥龍騰五百人守之。

translations.literal: The Liu clan and Chai then forged an edict saying Bin lacked a loyal, instructive heart, relieved him of office and sent him to his residence, and had Chai's younger brother Xiong lead five hundred Dragon Soarers to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu and Chai forged an edict charging Bin with disloyalty, stripped him of office, and confined him to his mansion under guard of five hundred Dragon Soarers led by Chai's brother Xiong.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，遵自幽州至鄴。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Zun arrived at Ye from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Zun arrived at Ye from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 敕朝堂受拜，配禁兵三萬遣之，遵涕泣而去。

translations.literal: An order that he receive homage in the audience hall and that thirty thousand palace guards be assigned to escort him; Zun departed weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to receive homage in the audience hall and given thirty thousand palace guards as escort; Zun left in tears.

sentences.zh: 是日，虎疾小瘳，問：「遵至末？」

translations.literal: That day Hu's illness improved slightly; he asked, "Has Zun arrived yet?"
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hu's condition improved slightly. He asked, "Has Zun arrived yet?"

sentences.zh: 左右對曰：「去已久矣。」

translations.literal: Those beside him answered, "He left long ago."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants replied, "He left long ago."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「恨不見之！」

translations.literal: Hu said, "I regret not having seen him!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "I regret not having seen him!"

sentences.zh: 虎臨西閣，龍騰中郎二百餘人列拜于前。

translations.literal: Hu came to the Western Pavilion; more than two hundred Dragon Soarer company commanders lined up to bow before him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu came to the Western Pavilion, where more than two hundred Dragon Soarer company commanders lined up to bow before him.

sentences.zh: 虎問：「何求？」

translations.literal: Hu asked, "What do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu asked, "What do you want?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「聖體不安，宜令燕王入宿衛，典兵馬。」

translations.literal: All said, "Your sacred person is unwell; the Prince of Yan should be brought in to guard the palace overnight and hold command of the armies."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Your Majesty is unwell. The Prince of Yan should be brought in to guard the palace and take command of the armies."

sentences.zh: 或言：「乞爲皇太子。」

translations.literal: Some said, "We beg that he be made crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Others said, "We beg that he be made crown prince."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「燕王不在內邪？

translations.literal: Hu said, "Is the Prince of Yan not inside?
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Is the Prince of Yan not here?

sentences.zh: 召以來！」

translations.literal: Summon him here!"
translations.idiomatic: Summon him at once!"

sentences.zh: 左右言：「王酒病，不能入。」

translations.literal: Those beside him said, "The prince suffers from wine-sickness and cannot enter."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "The prince is ill from wine and cannot come in."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「促持輦迎之，當付璽授。」

translations.literal: Hu said, "Hurry—have a carriage fetch him; I shall hand over the seal and credentials."
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Hurry—send a carriage for him. I will hand over the seal and regalia."

sentences.zh: 亦竟無行者。

translations.literal: Yet in the end no one went.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end no one went.

sentences.zh: 尋惛眩而入。

translations.literal: Before long he grew dazed and went inside.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he grew dazed and withdrew inside.

sentences.zh: 張豺使張雄矯詔殺斌。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai had Zhang Xiong forge an edict and kill Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai had Zhang Xiong forge an edict and execute Bin.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，劉氏復矯詔以豺爲太保、都督中外諸軍，錄尚書事，如霍光故事。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, the Liu clan again forged an edict making Chai Grand Preceptor, commander of all armies within and without, and Director of the Masters of Writing—following the precedent of Huo Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Empress Liu forged another edict appointing Chai Grand Preceptor, commander of all armies at court and in the field, and Director of the Masters of Writing—on the model of Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 侍中徐統嘆曰：「亂將作矣，吾無爲預之。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xu Tong sighed and said, "Disorder is about to break out; I will have no part in it."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xu Tong sighed and said, "Disorder is about to break out. I will have no part in it."

sentences.zh: 仰藥而死。

translations.literal: He took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 己巳，虎卒，太子世即位，尊劉氏爲皇太后。

translations.literal: On day jisi, Hu died; Crown Prince Shi succeeded to the throne and honored the Liu clan as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Shi Hu died. Crown Prince Shi took the throne and honored Empress Liu as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 劉氏臨朝稱制，以張豺爲丞相；

translations.literal: The Liu clan held court and exercised power in her own name, making Zhang Chai Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu held court and ruled in her own name, appointing Zhang Chai Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 豺辭不受，請以彭城王遵、義陽王鑒爲左右丞相，以慰其心，劉氏從之。

translations.literal: Chai declined and would not accept, requesting that Prince of Pengcheng Zun and Prince of Yiyang Jian be made left and right chancellors to set their hearts at ease; the Liu clan consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chai declined, asking instead that Prince Zun of Pengcheng and Prince Jian of Yiyang be named left and right chancellors to reassure them; Empress Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 豺與太尉張舉謀誅司空李農，舉素與農善，密告之；

translations.literal: Chai and Grand Commandant Zhang Ju plotted to kill Minister of Works Li Nong; Ju had always been on good terms with Nong and secretly informed him;
translations.idiomatic: Chai and Grand Commandant Zhang Ju plotted to kill Li Nong, Minister of Works. Ju had always been friendly with Nong and warned him in secret;

sentences.zh: 農奔廣宗，帥乞活數萬家保上白劉氏使張舉統宿衛諸軍圍之。

translations.literal: Nong fled to Guangzong and led tens of thousands of refugee families to hold Shangbai; the Liu clan had Zhang Ju command the palace guard armies to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Nong fled to Guangzong and led tens of thousands of refugee families to hold Shangbai; Empress Liu had Zhang Ju command the palace guards to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 豺以張離爲鎮軍大將軍，監中外諸軍事，以爲己副。

translations.literal: Chai made Zhang Li Grand General Who Guards the Army, overseer of all military affairs within and without, to serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Chai appointed Zhang Li Grand General Who Guards the Army and overseer of all armies at court and in the field, to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 彭城王遵至河內，聞喪；

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Zun reached Henei and heard of the bereavement;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zun of Pengcheng reached Henei and heard of the death;

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲、蒲洪、劉寧及征虜將軍石閔、武衛將軍王鸞等討梁犢還，遇遵于李城，共說遵曰：「殿下長且賢，先帝亦有意以殿下爲嗣；

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong, Pu Hong, Liu Ning, and Campaign General Shi Min, Martial Guard General Wang Luan, and others, returning from suppressing Liang Du, met Zun at Licheng. Together they urged Zun, saying, "Your Highness is elder and worthy; the late emperor also intended you as heir;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong, Pu Hong, Liu Ning, Campaign General Shi Min, Martial Guard General Wang Luan, and others, returning from the campaign against Liang Du, met Zun at Licheng. Together they urged him: "Your Highness is elder and worthy; the late emperor also meant you for the succession;

sentences.zh: 正以末年惛惑，爲張豺所誤。

translations.literal: it was only because in his last years he was confused and deluded that he was misled by Zhang Chai.
translations.idiomatic: it was only in his final years, confused and deluded, that Zhang Chai misled him.

sentences.zh: 今女主臨朝，奸臣用事，上白相持未下，京師宿衛空虛，殿下若聲張豺之罪，鼓行而討之，其誰不開門倒戈而迎殿下者！」

translations.literal: Now the empress rules from behind the curtain and wicked ministers hold power; the stalemate at Shangbai is not yet broken, and the capital's palace guards stand empty. If Your Highness proclaims Chai's crimes and marches to punish him, who will not throw open the gates and turn his blade to welcome you!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the empress rules from behind the curtain and wicked ministers hold sway. Shangbai still holds out, and the capital's palace guards stand empty. Proclaim Chai's crimes and march to punish him—who will not throw open the gates and turn his blade to welcome you!"

sentences.zh: 遵從之。

translations.literal: Zun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zun agreed.

sentences.zh: 五月，遵自李城舉兵，還趣鄴，洛州刺史劉國帥洛陽之衆往會之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Zun raised troops at Licheng and hastened back toward Ye; Inspector of Luozhou Liu Guo led the men of Luoyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zun raised his banner at Licheng and marched on Ye. Liu Guo, inspector of Luozhou, led the forces of Luoyang to join him.

sentences.zh: 檄至鄴，張豺大懼，馳召上白之軍。

translations.literal: When the proclamation reached Ye, Zhang Chai was terrified and hastily recalled the armies at Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: When Zun's proclamation reached Ye, Zhang Chai was terrified and urgently recalled the armies at Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，遵軍于蕩陰，戎卒九萬，石閔爲前鋒。

translations.literal: On day bingxu Zun encamped at Dangyin with ninety thousand armed men; Shi Min was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Zun encamped at Dangyin with ninety thousand troops; Shi Min led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 豺將出拒之，耆舊、羯士皆曰：「彭城王來奔喪，吾當出迎之，不能爲張豺守城也！」

translations.literal: Chai was about to march out to oppose him when the elders and Jie warriors all said, "Prince of Pengcheng comes to mourn— we ought to go out and welcome him; we cannot hold the city for Zhang Chai!"
translations.idiomatic: Chai was about to march out to meet him when the elders and Jie warriors all said, "Prince Zun of Pengcheng comes to mourn the dead—we must go out and welcome him. We will not hold the city for Zhang Chai!"

sentences.zh: 逾城而出；

translations.literal: They climbed over the walls and went out;
translations.idiomatic: They climbed over the walls and went out;

sentences.zh: 豺斬之，不能止。

translations.literal: Chai executed them but could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Chai had them executed but could not stop the exodus.

sentences.zh: 張離亦帥騰二千，斬關迎遵。

translations.literal: Zhang Li also led two thousand Dragon Soarers, cut the gates, and welcomed Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li also led two thousand Dragon Soarers, broke the gates, and welcomed Zun in.

sentences.zh: 劉氏懼，召張豺入，對之悲哭曰：「先帝梓宮未殯，而禍難至此！

translations.literal: The Liu clan was afraid; she summoned Zhang Chai in and weeping before him said, "The late emperor's coffin is not yet interred, and calamity has come to this pass!
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu was terrified. She summoned Zhang Chai and wept before him: "The late emperor's coffin is not yet interred, and calamity has come to this!

sentences.zh: 今嗣子沖幼，托之將軍，將軍將若之何？

translations.literal: The heir is young and frail; I entrust him to you, general—what will you do about it?
translations.idiomatic: The heir is young and frail. I entrust him to you, General—what will you do?

sentences.zh: 欲加遵重位，能弭之乎？」

translations.literal: If we grant Zun a high post, can that appease him?"
translations.idiomatic: If we grant Zun a high office, can that appease him?"

sentences.zh: 豺惶怖不知所出，但云「唯唯」。

translations.literal: Chai was terrified and knew not what to do; he could only say "yes, yes."
translations.idiomatic: Chai was terrified and knew not what to do; he could only murmur "yes, yes."

sentences.zh: 乃下詔，以遵爲丞相，領大司馬、大都督、督中外諸軍，錄尚書事，加黃鉞、九錫。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued making Zun Chancellor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commander, commander of all armies within and without, Director of the Masters of Writing, with the yellow axe and the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued naming Zun Chancellor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commander, commander of all armies at court and in the field, Director of the Masters of Writing, with the yellow axe and the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遵至安陽亭，張豺懼而出迎，遵命執之。

translations.literal: On day jichou Zun reached Anyang Pavilion; Zhang Chai, afraid, went out to welcome him; Zun ordered him seized.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Zun reached Anyang Pavilion. Zhang Chai, terrified, went out to welcome him; Zun ordered him seized.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，遵擐甲曜兵，入自鳳陽門，升太武前殿，擗踴盡哀，退如東閣。

translations.literal: On day gengyin Zun donned armor, displayed his troops, entered through Fengyang Gate, ascended the Hall of Martial Sovereignty, beat his breast and wept in full mourning, then withdrew to the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Zun donned armor, paraded his troops, entered through Fengyang Gate, ascended the Hall of Martial Sovereignty, beat his breast and wept in full mourning, then withdrew to the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 斬張豺于平樂市，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Zhang Chai was executed in the Pingle market and his three clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chai was executed in the Pingle market and his entire clan exterminated to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 假劉氏令曰：「嗣子幼沖，先帝私恩所授，皇業至重，非所克堪，其以遵嗣位。」

translations.literal: A forged order in the Liu clan's name said, "The heir is young and tender; the late emperor's private favor installed him. The imperial enterprise is too weighty for him to bear—let Zun succeed to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: A forged order in Empress Liu's name read: "The heir is young and frail, installed by the late emperor's private favor. The imperial enterprise is too weighty for him—let Zun succeed to the throne."

sentences.zh: 于是遵即位，大赦，罷上白之圍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zun took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and lifted the siege of Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zun took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and lifted the siege of Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，封世爲譙王，廢劉氏爲太妃，尋皆殺之。

translations.literal: On day xinmao Shi was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao; the Liu clan was demoted to Grand Consort, and soon both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Shi was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao; Empress Liu was demoted to Grand Consort, and soon both were killed.

sentences.zh: 李農來歸罪，使復其位。

translations.literal: Li Nong came to admit guilt and was restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong came to submit and was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 尊母鄭氏爲皇太后，立妃張氏爲皇后，故燕王斌子衍爲皇太子。

translations.literal: Zun honored his mother Lady Zheng as Empress Dowager, installed his consort Lady Zhang as empress, and made the late Prince of Yan Bin's son Yan crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zun honored his mother Lady Zheng as Empress Dowager, installed his consort Lady Zhang as empress, and made the late Prince Bin of Yan's son Yan crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以義陽王鑒爲侍中、太傅，沛王沖爲太保，樂平王苞爲大司馬，汝陰王琨爲大將軍，武興公閔爲都督中外諸軍事、輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Yiyang Jian was made Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor; Prince of Pei Chong Grand Preceptor; Prince of Leping Bao Grand Marshal; Prince of Runan Kun Grand General; Duke of Military Glory Min commander of all armies within and without and General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Yiyang became Palace Attendant and Grand Tutor; Prince Chong of Pei Grand Preceptor; Prince Bao of Leping Grand Marshal; Prince Kun of Runan Grand General; and Duke of Military Glory Min commander of all armies at court and in the field and General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 甲午，鄴中暴風拔樹，震雷，雨雹大如盂升。

translations.literal: On day jiawu in Ye a violent wind uprooted trees; thunder rolled, and hail as large as a basin and sheng fell.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu a violent wind uprooted trees in Ye; thunder rolled, and hailstones as large as basins fell.

sentences.zh: 太武輝華殿灾，及諸門觀閣蕩然無餘，乘輿服御，燒者太半，金石皆盡，火月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: The Hall of Martial Brilliance burned, and all gate towers and viewing pavilions were swept bare; carriages, regalia, and court dress—more than half burned; metal and stone were consumed to nothing; the fire took more than a month to die.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Martial Brilliance burned, and every gate tower and viewing pavilion was reduced to ashes; more than half the imperial carriages, regalia, and court dress were lost, metal and stone ornaments melted away, and the fire burned for more than a month before it died.

sentences.zh: 時沛王沖鎮薊，聞遵殺世自立，謂其僚佐曰：「世受先帝之命，遵輒廢而殺之，罪莫大焉！

translations.literal: Prince of Pei Chong was then garrisoning Ji. Hearing that Zun had killed Shi and seized the throne himself, he said to his staff, "Shi received the late emperor's mandate; Zun rashly deposed and killed him—no crime could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Pei was then garrisoning Ji. Hearing that Zun had killed Shi and seized the throne, he told his staff: "Shi held the late emperor's mandate. Zun rashly deposed and murdered him—no crime could be greater!

sentences.zh: 其敕內外戒嚴，孤將親討之。」

translations.literal: Issue orders within and without for strict guard; I shall personally campaign against him."
translations.idiomatic: Issue orders for strict guard throughout the realm. I shall campaign against him in person."

sentences.zh: 于是留寧北將軍沐堅戍幽州，帥衆五萬自薊南下，傳檄燕、趙，所在雲集；

translations.literal: Thereupon he left Northern Pacification General Mu Jian to hold Youzhou and led fifty thousand men south from Ji, dispatching proclamations through Yan and Zhao; everywhere men gathered like clouds;
translations.idiomatic: He left Northern Pacification General Mu Jian to hold Youzhou and led fifty thousand men south from Ji, dispatching proclamations through Yan and Zhao; men rallied to him everywhere;

sentences.zh: 比至常山，衆十餘萬，軍于苑鄉；

translations.literal: by the time he reached Changshan his host exceeded a hundred thousand; he encamped at Yuanxiang;
translations.idiomatic: by the time he reached Changshan his host exceeded a hundred thousand; he encamped at Yuanxiang;

sentences.zh: 遇遵赦書，沖曰：「皆吾弟也；

translations.literal: meeting Zun's amnesty edict, Chong said, "They are all my brothers;
translations.idiomatic: When he received Zun's amnesty edict, Chong said, "They are all my brothers;

sentences.zh: 死者不可復追，何爲復相殘乎！

translations.literal: the dead cannot be brought back—why must we slaughter one another again?
translations.idiomatic: the dead cannot be brought back—why must we slaughter one another again?

sentences.zh: 吾將歸矣！」

translations.literal: I am going home!"
translations.idiomatic: I am going home!"

sentences.zh: 其將陳暹曰：「彭城篡弑自尊，爲罪大矣！

translations.literal: His general Chen Xian said, "Prince of Pengcheng usurped the throne and murdered the sovereign—a crime of the first magnitude!
translations.idiomatic: His general Chen Xian said, "Prince Zun of Pengcheng usurped the throne and murdered the sovereign—a crime of the first magnitude!

sentences.zh: 王雖北旆，臣將南轅。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness turns your banners north, your servant will drive south.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Highness turns north, your servant will march south.

sentences.zh: 俟平京師，擒彭城，然後奉迎大駕。」

translations.literal: Wait until we pacify the capital, capture the Prince of Pengcheng, and then escort the imperial carriage in welcome."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until we pacify the capital, capture Prince Zun of Pengcheng, and then escort the imperial carriage in welcome."

sentences.zh: 沖乃復進。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon advanced again.
translations.idiomatic: Chong thereupon advanced again.

sentences.zh: 遵馳遣王擢以書喻沖，沖弗聽。

translations.literal: Zun hastily sent Wang Zhuo with a letter to persuade Chong; Chong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zun hastily sent Wang Zhuo with a letter to persuade Chong, but Chong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 遵使武興公閔及李農等帥精卒十萬討之，戰于平棘，沖兵大敗。

translations.literal: Zun sent Duke of Military Glory Min and Li Nong and others with a hundred thousand picked troops against him; they fought at Pingji and Chong's army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zun sent Duke of Military Glory Min and Li Nong with a hundred thousand picked troops against him. They fought at Pingji and Chong's army was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 獲沖于元氏，賜死，坑其士卒三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Chong was taken at Yuanshi, granted death by suicide, and his soldiers more than thirty thousand were buried alive in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was captured at Yuanshi, granted death by suicide, and more than thirty thousand of his soldiers were buried alive in a pit.

sentences.zh: 武興公閔言于遵曰：「蒲洪，人杰也；

translations.literal: Duke of Military Glory Min said to Zun, "Pu Hong is a man among men;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Military Glory Min said to Zun, "Pu Hong is a man among men;

sentences.zh: 今以洪鎮關中，臣恐秦、雍之地非復國家之有。

translations.literal: now that Hong guards the passes of the west, I fear Qin and Yong will no longer belong to the state.
translations.idiomatic: now that he holds the western passes, I fear Qin and Yong will slip from the state's grasp.

sentences.zh: 此雖先帝臨終之命，然陛下踐祚，自宜改圖。」

translations.literal: Though this was the late emperor's deathbed command, now that Your Majesty has ascended the throne you ought to change the plan."
translations.idiomatic: Though that was the late emperor's deathbed command, now that Your Majesty reigns you ought to change course."

sentences.zh: 遵從之，罷洪都督，餘如前制。

translations.literal: Zun agreed, stripped Hong of his command as governor, and left the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zun agreed, stripped Hong of his command over the western provinces, and left his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 洪怒，歸枋頭，遣使來降。

translations.literal: Hong was enraged, returned to Fangtou, and sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was enraged. He withdrew to Fangtou and sent envoys to offer his surrender.

sentences.zh: 燕平狄將軍慕容霸上書于燕王俊曰：「石虎窮凶極暴，天之所弃，餘燼僅存，自相魚肉。

translations.literal: Murong Ba, General Who Pacifies the Di, memorialized Murong Jun, saying, "Shi Hu exhausts cruelty to the utmost; Heaven has abandoned him. Ember alone remains, and they tear one another like fish in a drying pool.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ba, General Who Pacifies the Di, memorialized Murong Jun: "Shi Hu has exhausted every cruelty; Heaven has abandoned him. Only embers remain, and they tear one another apart like fish in a drying pool.

sentences.zh: 今中國倒懸，企望仁恤，若大軍一振，勢必投戈。」

translations.literal: Now the Central Land hangs upside down and longs for benevolent relief; if our great army stirs once, they will surely cast aside their weapons."
translations.idiomatic: The Central Land hangs in peril and longs for benevolent rule. If our great army stirs once, they will surely cast down their weapons."

sentences.zh: 北平太守孫興亦表言：「石氏大亂，宜以時進取中原。」

translations.literal: Administrator of Beiping Sun Xing also memorialized, saying, "The Shi house is in great disorder; it is time to advance and seize the Central Land."
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Beiping Sun Xing also memorialized: "The Shi house is in chaos. The time has come to advance into the Central Land."

sentences.zh: 俊以新遭大喪，弗許。

translations.literal: Jun, having newly suffered a great bereavement, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, still in mourning for a recent bereavement, refused.

sentences.zh: 霸馳詣龍城，言于俊曰：「難得而易失者，時也。

translations.literal: Ba galloped to Longcheng and said to Jun, "What is hard to obtain and easy to lose is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Ba galloped to Longcheng and said to Jun, "Opportunity is hard to seize and easy to lose.

sentences.zh: 萬一石氏衰而復興，或有英雄據其成資，豈惟失此大利，亦恐更爲後患。」

translations.literal: If by chance the Shi house declines yet revives, or some hero seizes its established resources, would we not only lose this great profit but also fear further trouble afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Shi house should rally from decline, or some hero seize the foundations they have already built, we would lose not only this great prize but invite a worse enemy for the future."

sentences.zh: 俊曰：「鄴中雖亂，鄧恒據安樂，兵强糧足，今若伐趙，東道不可由也，當由盧龍；

translations.literal: Jun said, "Though Ye is in disorder, Deng Heng holds Anle with strong troops and ample grain. If we campaign against Zhao now, the eastern route cannot be used; we must go by Lulong;
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Ye may be in chaos, but Deng Heng holds Anle with strong troops and full granaries. If we strike Zhao now, the eastern road is closed to us; we must take the Lulong route;

sentences.zh: 盧龍山徑險狹，虜乘高斷要，首尾爲患，將若之何？」

translations.literal: the mountain paths of Lulong are perilous and narrow; the enemy will hold the heights and cut the passes, and we will be harried front and rear—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: the Lulong passes are narrow and treacherous. The enemy can hold the heights and choke the defiles, trapping us between front and rear. What then?"

sentences.zh: 霸曰：「恒雖欲爲石氏拒守，其將士顧家，人懷歸志，若大軍臨之，自然瓦解。

translations.literal: Ba said, "Though Heng wishes to hold out for the Shi house, his officers and soldiers think of their homes; every man harbors a mind to return. If a great army presses them, they will naturally collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "Heng may wish to hold the line for the Shi house, but his men long for home. If our main force appears, they will fall apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 臣請爲殿下前驅，東出徒河，潜趣令支，出其不意，彼聞之，勢必震駭，上不過閉門自守，下不免弃城逃潰，何暇禦我哉！

translations.literal: Your servant asks to serve Your Highness as vanguard: march east out of Tuhe, steal swiftly on Lingzhi, and take them unawares. When they hear of it they will surely be shaken with terror—at best they will only shut their gates and hold themselves in; at worst they cannot escape abandoning their cities and fleeing in rout. How would they have leisure to resist us!
translations.idiomatic: Let me lead the van: strike east from Tuhe, slip swiftly on Lingzhi, and catch them unaware. News of us will terrify them—at best they bar their gates; at worst they abandon their posts and flee. They will have no time to oppose us!

sentences.zh: 然則殿下可以安步而前，無復留難矣。」

translations.literal: Then Your Highness may advance at an easy pace, and there will be no further obstruction."
translations.idiomatic: Then Your Highness may advance at leisure, with no further obstacle in your path."

sentences.zh: 俊猶豫未决，以問五材將軍封弈，對曰：「用兵之道，敵强則用智，敵弱則用勢。

translations.literal: Jun hesitated and could not decide; he asked General of the Five Talents Feng Yi, who replied, "The way of employing troops: when the enemy is strong, use stratagem; when the enemy is weak, use momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Jun still hesitated. He consulted Feng Yi, General of the Five Talents, who answered, "In war, use cunning against a strong foe and momentum against a weak one.

sentences.zh: 是故以大吞小，猶狼之食豚也；

translations.literal: Thus the great devouring the small is like a wolf eating a piglet;
translations.idiomatic: The great swallowing the small is like a wolf taking a piglet;

sentences.zh: 以治易亂，猶日之消雪也。

translations.literal: order replacing disorder is like the sun melting snow.
translations.idiomatic: order replacing chaos is like sunlight melting snow.

sentences.zh: 大王自上世以來，積德累仁，兵强士練。

translations.literal: Great King, from generations past you have heaped up virtue and accumulated benevolence; your troops are strong and your soldiers well trained.
translations.idiomatic: Great King, your house has piled up virtue for generations. Your armies are strong and your soldiers seasoned.

sentences.zh: 石虎極其殘暴，死未瞑目，子孫爭國，上下乖亂。

translations.literal: Shi Hu exhausted cruelty to the utmost; he had not closed his eyes in death before sons and grandsons fought over the realm, and high and low were torn apart in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu drove cruelty to its limit. Hardly had he closed his eyes before his kin tore the realm apart, and court and camp alike fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 中國之民，墜于塗炭，廷頸企踵以待振拔，大王若揚兵南邁，先取薊城，次指鄴都，宣耀威德，懷撫遺民，彼孰不扶老提幼以迎大王？

translations.literal: The people of the Central Land have fallen into fire and charcoal; they stretch their necks and stand on tiptoe awaiting deliverance. If Great King raises your banners and marches south, first take Ji, then point at Ye, proclaiming your majesty and virtue and cherishing the survivors—who among them would not lead the old by the hand and carry the young to welcome Great King?
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Central Land lie in ashes. They crane their necks and rise on tiptoe, waiting to be lifted from ruin. March south, take Ji first and Ye next, proclaim your power and mercy, and comfort those who remain—who would not come forth, old and young together, to welcome you?

sentences.zh: 凶黨將望旗冰碎，安能爲害乎！」

translations.literal: The vicious faction will see your banners and shatter like ice—how could they do harm!"
translations.idiomatic: The wicked will melt like ice at sight of your banners. What harm can they do!"

sentences.zh: 從事中郎黃泓曰：「今太白經天，歲集畢北，天下易主，陰國受命，此必然之驗也，宜速出師，以承天意。」

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Huang Hong said, "Now Venus crosses the heavens, and the year star gathers north of Bi; the realm will change its lord, and the northern state receives the Mandate. This is a sure sign. You should march swiftly to take up Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Huang Hong said, "Venus crosses the sky, and Jupiter gathers north of Bi—the realm will change hands, and the northern state is destined to rule. The omen is plain. March at once and answer Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 折沖將軍慕輿根曰：「中國之民困于石氏之亂，咸思易主以救湯火之急，此千載一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: General Who Breaks the Foe Murong Gen said, "The people of the Central Land are afflicted by the disorder of the Shi house; all long for a change of lord to rescue them from the urgency of boiling water and raging fire. This is a moment once in a thousand years—it must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Breaks the Foe Murong Gen said, "The Central Land groans under Shi chaos. Every man yearns for a new ruler to pull him from the fire. Such a moment comes once in a thousand years. Do not let it pass.

sentences.zh: 自武宣王以來，招賢養民，務農訓兵，正俟今日。

translations.literal: Since Martial-Propagating King, you have recruited the worthy, nurtured the people, devoted yourself to agriculture, and drilled the troops—all precisely awaiting this day.
translations.idiomatic: Since Martial-Propagating King, you have gathered talent, nurtured the people, tilled the fields, and trained the army—all for this day.

sentences.zh: 今時至不取，更復顧慮，豈天意未欲使海內平定邪，將大王不欲取天下也？」

translations.literal: Now the time has come and you do not seize it; you hesitate again—is it that Heaven does not yet wish the realm within the seas pacified, or that Great King does not wish to take the world?"
translations.idiomatic: The hour is here, yet you hold back. Does Heaven not yet wish the realm united—or does Great King not wish to take the world?"

sentences.zh: 俊笑而從之。

translations.literal: Jun smiled and followed their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Jun smiled and agreed.

sentences.zh: 以慕容恪爲輔國將軍，慕容評爲輔弼將軍，左長史陽鶩爲輔義將軍，謂之「三輔」。

translations.literal: He appointed Murong Ke General Who Assists the State, Murong Ping General Who Assists the Throne, and Left Chief Clerk Yang Wu General Who Assists Righteousness—they were called the "Three Assistants."
translations.idiomatic: He made Murong Ke General Who Assists the State, Murong Ping General Who Assists the Throne, and Left Chief Clerk Yang Wu General Who Assists Righteousness—the "Three Assistants."

sentences.zh: 慕容霸爲前鋒都督、建鋒將軍。

translations.literal: Murong Ba was made Vanguard Commander-in-Chief and General Who Establishes the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ba became Vanguard Commander-in-Chief and General Who Establishes the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 選精兵二十餘萬，講武戒嚴，爲進取之計。

translations.literal: He selected more than two hundred thousand elite troops, reviewed arms, and imposed strict guard, making plans for advance.
translations.idiomatic: He chose more than two hundred thousand picked troops, drilled them under strict guard, and laid plans for the advance.

sentences.zh: 六月，葬趙王虎于顯原陵，謚曰武帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zhao King Hu was buried at Xianyuan Mausoleum; his posthumous title was Emperor Wu, and his temple name was Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhao King Hu was buried at Xianyuan Mausoleum with the posthumous title Emperor Wu and temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 桓溫聞趙亂，出屯安陸，遣諸將經營北方。

translations.literal: Huan Wen, hearing of disorder in Zhao, went out and encamped at Anlu, dispatching his generals to manage affairs in the north.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen heard of chaos in Zhao, he encamped at Anlu and sent his generals to seize openings in the north.

sentences.zh: 趙揚州刺史王浹舉壽春降，西中郎將陳逵進據壽春。

translations.literal: Zhao's Inspector of Yangzhou Wang Yi raised Shouchun in surrender; Western Gentleman-of-the-Guard Chen Kui advanced and occupied Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Inspector of Yangzhou Wang Yi surrendered Shouchun. Western Gentleman-of-the-Guard Chen Kui marched in and took the city.

sentences.zh: 征北大將軍褚裒上表請伐趙，即日戒嚴，直指泗口，朝議以裒事任貴重，不宜深入，宜先遣偏師。

translations.literal: Northern Expeditionary Grand General Chu Pou memorialized requesting a campaign against Zhao; that same day strict guard was imposed, aiming straight for Sikou. Court discussion held that Pou's commission was weighty and he ought not penetrate deeply; a detached force should be sent first.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Expeditionary Grand General Chu Pou memorialized to attack Zhao. That same day the army went on alert and marched for Sikou. The court argued that Pou's rank was too weighty for a deep thrust and that a vanguard should go first.

sentences.zh: 裒奏言：「前已遣前鋒督護王頤之等徑造彭城，後遣督護麋嶷進據下邳。

translations.literal: Pou memorialized, "Previously I sent Vanguard Commander Wang Yizhi and others straight to Pengcheng, and afterward sent Commander Mi Yi to advance and hold Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Pou replied, "I have already sent Vanguard Commander Wang Yizhi straight to Pengcheng and Commander Mi Yi to seize Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 今宜速發，以成聲勢。」

translations.literal: Now we should march swiftly to complete our momentum."
translations.idiomatic: The main body should move now to give those gains weight."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，加裒征討大都督，督徐、兗、青、揚、豫五州諸軍事，裒帥衆三萬，徑赴彭城，北方士民降附者日以千計。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Pou was made Grand Commander for Campaign and Punishment, overseeing military affairs of Xu, Yan, Qing, Yang, and Yu; Pou led thirty thousand men straight to Pengcheng, and northerners who surrendered and attached themselves numbered thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Pou was made Grand Commander for Campaign and Punishment over Xu, Yan, Qing, Yang, and Yu. He led thirty thousand men to Pengcheng, and northerners who came over to Jin numbered thousands a day.

sentences.zh: 朝野皆以爲中原指期可復，光祿大夫蔡謨獨謂所親曰：「胡滅誠爲大慶，然恐更貽朝廷之憂。」

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike thought the Central Plain could be recovered within a set term; Grandee of Splendid Happiness Cai Mo alone told those close to him, "The destruction of the barbarians is truly a great rejoicing, yet I fear it will bring fresh worry upon the court."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike believed the Central Plain would soon be recovered. Only Grandee of Splendid Happiness Cai Mo told his intimates, "The fall of the barbarians is a true blessing, yet I fear it will bring the court a new grief."

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: The man said, "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: His companion asked, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 謨曰：』夫能順天乘時，濟群生于艱難者，非上聖與英雄不能爲也，自餘則莫若度德量力。

translations.literal: Mo said, "He who can follow Heaven and ride the times, delivering the multitude from hardship—none but a supreme sage or a hero can do this; for the rest, nothing surpasses measuring virtue and gauging strength.
translations.idiomatic: Mo said, "Only a supreme sage or a true hero can follow Heaven's season and rescue the people from calamity. For anyone else, the wiser course is to measure one's virtue against the task and one's strength against the foe.

sentences.zh: 觀今日之事，殆非時賢所及，必將經營分表，疲民以逞；

translations.literal: Viewing affairs today, they are scarcely within the reach of the worthies of the age; they will surely scheme for separate domains and exhaust the people to gratify their ambitions;
translations.idiomatic: Look at what passes for talent today. None of it measures up. They will carve out private domains and grind the people down to feed their ambitions;

sentences.zh: 既而材略疏短，不能副心，財殫力竭，智勇俱困，安得不憂及朝廷乎！

translations.literal: then their talent and strategy will prove shallow and short, unable to match their hearts; wealth spent and strength exhausted, wit and courage alike trapped—how could worry not reach the court!"
translations.idiomatic: then their shallow gifts will fail their grand designs. Funds will run dry, strength will fail, wit and courage alike will be spent—how could the court escape the cost!"

sentences.zh: 魯郡民五百餘家相與起兵附晋，求援于褚裒，裒遣部將王龕、李邁將銳卒三千迎之。

translations.literal: More than five hundred households in Lu commandery together raised troops to attach themselves to Jin and sought aid from Chu Pou; Pou sent his subordinates Wang Kan and Li Mai with three thousand crack troops to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred households in Lu commandery rose together for Jin and begged Chu Pou for aid. Pou sent Wang Kan and Li Mai with three thousand picked troops to meet them.

sentences.zh: 趙南討大都督李農帥騎二萬與龕等戰于代陂，龕等大敗，皆沒于趙。

translations.literal: Zhao's Grand Commander for Southern Punishment Li Nong led twenty thousand horse and fought Kan and the others at Daipo; Kan and the rest were utterly defeated and all perished in Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Grand Commander for Southern Punishment Li Nong met them at Daipo with twenty thousand cavalry. Kan's force was shattered; every man was lost to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 八月，裒退屯廣陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Pou withdrew and encamped at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Pou withdrew to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 陳逵聞之，焚壽春積聚，毀城遁還。
