translations.literal: Chen Kui, hearing of it, burned Shouchun's stores, destroyed the walls, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Kui heard, he burned Shouchun's stores, dismantled the defenses, and fled south.

sentences.zh: 裒上疏乞自貶，詔不許，命裒還鎮京口，解征討都督。

translations.literal: Pou memorialized asking to demote himself; the edict did not permit it but ordered Pou to return and hold Jingkou, relieving him of the post of campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: Pou asked to be demoted. The throne refused but ordered him back to Jingkou and stripped him of his campaign command.

sentences.zh: 時河北大亂，遺民二十餘萬口渡河欲來歸附，會裒已還，威勢不接，皆不能自拔，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: At that time the north of the Yellow River was in great disorder; more than two hundred thousand surviving people crossed the river wishing to come over to Jin, but as Pou had already returned, his prestige and force did not reach them, and none could extricate themselves—death took nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: The north of the Yellow River was in chaos. More than two hundred thousand refugees tried to cross the river to Jin, but Pou had already withdrawn and Jin's power no longer reached them. None could escape; nearly all perished.

sentences.zh: 趙樂平王苞謀帥關右之衆攻鄴，左長史石光、司馬曹曜等固諫，苞怒，殺光等百餘人。

translations.literal: Zhao's Prince of Le Ping Bao plotted to lead the hosts of the western passes against Ye; Left Chief Clerk Shi Guang, Marshal Cao Yao, and others firmly remonstrated; Bao was enraged and killed Guang and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Prince of Le Ping Bao planned to march the armies of the western passes on Ye. Left Chief Clerk Shi Guang and Marshal Cao Yao urged him to desist. Bao flew into a rage and killed Guang and more than a hundred besides.

sentences.zh: 苞性貪而無謀，雍州豪杰知其無成，幷遣使告晋，梁州刺史司馬勛帥衆赴之。

translations.literal: Bao was greedy by nature and without strategy; the stalwarts of Yongzhou knew he would not succeed and together sent envoys to inform Jin; Inspector of Liangzhou Sima Xun led his host to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was greedy and witless. The magnates of Yongzhou saw he would fail and sent envoys together to Jin. Inspector of Liangzhou Sima Xun marched to their aid.

sentences.zh: 楊初襲趙西城，破之。

translations.literal: Yang Chu raided Zhao's western city and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chu raided Zhao's western city and took it.

sentences.zh: 九月，凉州官屬共上張重華爲丞相、凉王、雍、秦、凉三州牧。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the officials of Liangzhou together elevated Zhang Chonghua as Chancellor, King of Liang, and Governor of the Three Provinces of Yong, Qin, and Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the officials of Liangzhou together made Zhang Chonghua Chancellor, King of Liang, and Governor of Yong, Qin, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 重華屢以錢帛賜左右寵臣；

translations.literal: Chonghua repeatedly bestowed coin and silk on favored attendants at his side;
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua showered coin and silk on the favorites at his side;

sentences.zh: 又喜博弈，頗廢政事。

translations.literal: he also delighted in gambling and greatly neglected government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: he took to gambling and neglected government affairs.

sentences.zh: 從事索振諫曰：「先王夙夜勤儉以實府庫，正以仇耻未雪，志平海內故也。

translations.literal: Attendant Suo Zhen remonstrated, saying, "The former king toiled day and night in diligence and frugality to fill the treasuries—precisely because national shame was not yet washed away and his will was to pacify the realm within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Suo Zhen remonstrated: "The former king labored day and night in thrift to fill the treasuries—because our shame was not yet avenged and his aim was to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 殿下嗣位之初，强寇侵逼，賴重餌之故，得戰士死力，僅保社稷。

translations.literal: When Your Highness first succeeded to the throne, strong enemies pressed upon us; only by heavy rewards did we obtain the warriors' death-defying effort and barely preserve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Highness first took the throne, powerful enemies pressed in. Only heavy rewards bought the soldiers' utmost loyalty and barely preserved the realm.

sentences.zh: 今蓄積已虛而寇仇尚在，豈可輕有耗散，以與無功之人乎！

translations.literal: Now stores are already empty while the enemy remains—how can you lightly squander and give to men without merit!
translations.idiomatic: The coffers are empty and the enemy still stands. How can you squander treasure on men who have earned nothing!

sentences.zh: 昔漢光、武躬親萬機，章奏詣闕，報不終日，故能隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Guangwu of Han personally attended to the myriad duties; memorials arriving at court received reply within the day—thus he could raise the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han handled every affair in person; memorials that reached court were answered the same day. That is how he restored the Han.

sentences.zh: 今章奏停滯，動經時月，下情不得上通，沉冤困于囹圄，殆非明主之事也。」

translations.literal: Now memorials stall for months on end; sentiment below cannot reach above; sunken wrongs languish in prison—this is scarcely the conduct of an enlightened lord."
translations.idiomatic: Now memorials lie idle for months. Grievances below never reach you; the wrongfully imprisoned rot in their cells. This is scarcely how an enlightened ruler governs."

sentences.zh: 重華謝之。

translations.literal: Chonghua apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua apologized.

sentences.zh: 司馬勛出駱谷，破趙長城戍，壁于懸鈎，去長安二百里，使治中劉煥攻長安，斬京兆太守劉秀離，又拔賀城；

translations.literal: Sima Xun marched out through Luogu, broke Zhao's Great Wall garrison, and fortified at Xuandiao two hundred li from Chang'an; he sent Administrator Liu Huan to attack Chang'an, beheaded Governor of Jingzhao Liu Xiuli, and also took Hecheng;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun marched through Luogu, smashed Zhao's Great Wall garrison, and fortified at Xuandiao two hundred li from Chang'an. He sent Administrator Liu Huan against Chang'an; Liu beheaded Governor of Jingzhao Liu Xiuli and took Hecheng;

sentences.zh: 三輔豪杰多殺守令以應勛，凡三十餘壁，衆五萬人。

translations.literal: many stalwarts of the Three Adjuncts killed their prefects and magistrates to answer Xun; in all more than thirty fortified camps, with a host of fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: magnates of the Three Adjuncts killed their local officials to join him—more than thirty fortified camps and fifty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 趙樂平王苞乃輟攻鄴之謀，使其將麻秋、姚國等將兵拒勛。

translations.literal: Zhao's Prince of Le Ping Bao thereupon set aside his plan to attack Ye and sent his generals Ma Qiu, Yao Guo, and others to lead troops against Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Le Ping Bao abandoned his march on Ye and sent Ma Qiu, Yao Guo, and others to block Xun.

sentences.zh: 趙主遵遣車騎將軍王朗帥精騎二萬以討勛爲名，因劫苞送鄴。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Zun sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Lang with twenty thousand picked horse in the name of campaigning against Xun, and on the way seized Bao and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ruler Zun sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Lang with twenty thousand picked cavalry, ostensibly to crush Xun but in truth to seize Bao and haul him back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 勛兵少，畏朗，不敢進。

translations.literal: Xun's troops were few; he feared Lang and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's force was too small. He feared Lang and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，釋懸鈎，拔宛城，殺趙南陽太守袁景，復還梁州。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, he abandoned Xuandiao, took Wancheng, killed Zhao's Administrator of Nanyang Yuan Jing, and returned again to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, he abandoned Xuandiao, took Wancheng, killed Zhao's Administrator of Nanyang Yuan Jing, and withdrew to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，趙主遵之發李城也，謂武興公閔曰：「努力！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao's ruler Zun set out from Licheng, he said to Duke of Military Glory Min, "Strive hard!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhao's ruler Zun marched from Licheng, he told Duke of Military Glory Min, "Fight hard!

sentences.zh: 事成，以爾爲太子。」

translations.literal: When the affair succeeds, I will make you heir."
translations.idiomatic: Succeed, and I will make you heir."

sentences.zh: 既而立太子衍。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he installed Yan as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward he made Yan crown prince instead.

sentences.zh: 閔恃功。

translations.literal: Min relied on his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Min counted on his service.

sentences.zh: 欲專朝政，遵不聽。

translations.literal: He wished to monopolize court government; Zun would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to dominate the court; Zun refused.

sentences.zh: 閔素驍勇，屢立戰功，夷、夏宿將皆憚之。

translations.literal: Min had always been fierce and brave, repeatedly achieving battle merit; veteran generals, barbarian and Chinese alike, all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Min was fierce in battle and had won victory after victory; veteran generals, Di and Chinese alike, feared him.

sentences.zh: 既爲都督，總內外兵權，乃撫循殿中將士，皆奏爲殿中員外將軍，爵關外侯。

translations.literal: Once he became commander-in-chief and held military authority within and without, he soothed and won over the palace guards, memorializing that all be made Extraordinary Generals of the Palace with the rank of Marquis Outside the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: As commander-in-chief he held all military power. He courted the palace guards, had each named Extraordinary General of the Palace, and ennobled them as marquises outside the passes.

sentences.zh: 遵弗之疑，而更題名善惡以挫抑之，衆咸怨怒。

translations.literal: Zun did not suspect him but instead marked names good and bad to check and suppress them; the multitude all resented in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Zun suspected nothing, yet graded the guards' names as good or bad to rein them in. They seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 中書令孟准、左衛將軍王鸞勸遵稍奪閔兵權，閔益恨望，准等咸勸誅之。

translations.literal: Chief of the Secretariat Meng Zhun and General of the Left Guard Wang Luan urged Zun gradually to strip Min of military authority; Min grew ever more resentful and full of longing for revenge, and Zhun and the rest all urged executing him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of the Secretariat Meng Zhun and General of the Left Guard Wang Luan urged Zun to pare back Min's command. Min's hatred deepened, and Zhun and his allies pressed for his death.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遵召義陽王鑒、樂平王苞、汝陽王琨、淮南王昭等入議于鄭太后前，曰：「閔不臣之迹漸著，今欲誅之，如何？」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zun summoned the Prince of Yiyang Jian, Prince of Le Ping Bao, Prince of Ruyang Kun, Prince of Huainan Zhao, and others to deliberate before Empress Dowager Zheng, saying, "Min's traces of disloyalty grow plain; I wish to execute him now—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zun summoned Princes Jian of Yiyang, Bao of Le Ping, Kun of Ruyang, Zhao of Huainan, and others to counsel before Empress Dowager Zheng: "Min's treason grows plain. I mean to kill him. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 鑒等皆曰：「宜然！」

translations.literal: Jian and the rest all said, "It should be so!"
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "It must be done!"

sentences.zh: 鄭氏曰：「李城還兵，無棘奴，豈有今日！

translations.literal: Lady Zheng said, "When the army returned from Licheng, without Jinu, how could there be today!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng said, "When the army returned from Licheng, without Jinu, would you sit on the throne today?

sentences.zh: 小驕縱之，何可遽殺！」

translations.literal: He is a little proud and indulgent—how can you kill him so hastily!"
translations.idiomatic: He is proud, yes, but only a little unruly. Why kill him in haste!"

sentences.zh: 鑒出，遣宦者楊環馳以告閔。

translations.literal: Jian went out and sent the eunuch Yang Huan galloping to inform Min.
translations.idiomatic: Jian left and sent the eunuch Yang Huan galloping to warn Min.

sentences.zh: 閔遂劫李農及右衛將軍王基密謀廢遵，使將軍蘇彥、周成帥甲士三千人執遵于南臺。

translations.literal: Min thereupon seized Li Nong and General of the Right Guard Wang Ji to plot secretly to depose Zun, and sent Generals Su Yan and Zhou Cheng with three thousand armored troops to seize Zun at the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Min then seized Li Nong and General of the Right Guard Wang Ji and plotted to depose Zun. He sent Generals Su Yan and Zhou Cheng with three thousand armored men to take Zun at the Southern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 遵方與婦人彈棋，問成曰：「反者誰也？」

translations.literal: Zun was just then playing pitch-pot with women and asked Cheng, "Who rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Zun was playing pitch-pot with his women when they seized him. He asked Cheng, "Who rebels?"

sentences.zh: 成曰：「義陽王鑒當立。」

translations.literal: Cheng said, "Prince of Yiyang Jian is to be enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Prince Jian of Yiyang is to be enthroned."

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「我尚如是，鑒能幾時！」

translations.literal: Zun said, "If I am still like this, how long can Jian last!"
translations.idiomatic: Zun said, "If I end like this, how long will Jian last!"

sentences.zh: 遂殺之于琨華殿，幷殺鄭太后、張后、太子衍、孟准、王鸞及上光祿張斐。

translations.literal: He was then killed in Kunhua Hall, together with Empress Dowager Zheng, Empress Zhang, Crown Prince Yan, Meng Zhun, Wang Luan, and Senior Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him in Kunhua Hall, together with Empress Dowager Zheng, Empress Zhang, Crown Prince Yan, Meng Zhun, Wang Luan, and Senior Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 鑒即位，大赦。

translations.literal: Jian ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以武興公閔爲大將軍，封武德王，司空李農爲大司馬，幷錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He made Duke of Military Glory Min Grand General and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wude; Minister of Works Li Nong was made Grand Marshal and concurrently Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He made Min Grand General and Prince of Wude, and Li Nong Grand Marshal with concurrent charge of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 郎闓爲司空，秦州刺史劉群爲尚書左僕射，侍中盧諶爲中書監。

translations.literal: Lang Kan was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Qinzhou Liu Qun was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Palace Attendant Lu Chen was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Kan became Minister of Works, Liu Qun of Qinzhou became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Palace Attendant Lu Chen became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秦、雍流民相帥西歸，路由枋頭，共推蒲洪爲主，衆至十餘萬。

translations.literal: Displaced people of Qin and Yong led one another westward in return; their route passed Fangtou, and together they made Pu Hong their leader—a host reaching more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees of Qin and Yong marched west together. Their road passed Fangtou, where they acclaimed Pu Hong as leader—a host of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 洪子健在鄴，斬關出奔枋頭。

translations.literal: Hong's son Jian was at Ye; he cut through the passes and fled out to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Jian was at Ye. He broke through the gates and fled to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼洪之逼，欲以計遣之，乃以洪爲都督關中諸軍事、征西大將軍、雍州牧、領秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian feared Hong's pressure and wished to send him off by stratagem; he therefore made Hong Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the passes of the west, Western Expeditionary Grand General, Governor of Yongzhou, and concurrent Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feared Hong's approach and tried to send him away with honors: Commander-in-Chief of the western passes, Western Expeditionary Grand General, Governor of Yongzhou, and concurrent Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪會官屬，議應受與不；

translations.literal: Hong gathered his officials and debated whether to accept or not;
translations.idiomatic: Hong gathered his officers to debate whether to accept;

sentences.zh: 主簿程樸請且與趙連和，如列國分境而治。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Cheng Pu asked first to ally with Zhao and rule divided realms like the feudal states of old.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Cheng Pu urged a temporary alliance with Zhao, each ruling his own domain like the old feudal states.

sentences.zh: 洪怒曰：「吾不堪爲天子邪？

translations.literal: Hong raged and said, "Am I unfit to be Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Hong raged. "Am I unfit to be Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 而-{云}-列國乎！」

translations.literal: And be merely one of the feudal states!"
translations.idiomatic: And you would have me settle for a mere regional kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 引樸斬之。

translations.literal: He had Pu brought forth and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He had Pu executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 都鄉元穆侯褚裒還至京口，聞哭聲甚多，以問左右，對曰：「皆代陂死者之家也。」

translations.literal: Chu Pou, Marquis Yuanmu of Duxiang, returned to Jingkou and heard a great many sounds of weeping; he asked those at his side, who replied, "They are all families of the dead at Daipo."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou, Marquis Yuanmu of Duxiang, returned to Jingkou to a chorus of mourning. He asked his attendants, who said, "These are the families of the men lost at Daipo."

sentences.zh: 裒慚憤發疾；

translations.literal: Pou, ashamed and enraged, fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: Shame and rage brought on an illness;

sentences.zh: 十二月，己酉，卒。

translations.literal: in the twelfth month, on the day jiyou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month, on the day jiyou, he died.

sentences.zh: 以吳國內史荀羨爲使持節、監徐、兗二州、揚州之晋陵諸軍事、徐州刺史，時年二十八，中興方伯未有如羨之少者。

translations.literal: Internal Administrator of Wu Xun Xian was made Bearer of the Staff, overseer of military affairs of Xu and Yan and of Jincheng in Yangzhou, and Inspector of Xuzhou; he was twenty-eight years old—since the Restoration no regional commander had been so young.
translations.idiomatic: Internal Administrator of Wu Xun Xian was made Bearer of the Staff, overseer of Xu and Yan and of Jincheng in Yangzhou, and Inspector of Xuzhou. He was twenty-eight—the youngest regional commander since the Restoration.

sentences.zh: 趙主鑒使樂平王苞、中書令李松、殿中將軍張才夜攻石閔、李農于琨華殿，不克，禁中擾亂。

translations.literal: Zhao's ruler Jian sent Prince of Le Ping Bao, Chief of the Secretariat Li Song, and General of the Palace Zhang Cai by night to attack Shi Min and Li Nong in Kunhua Hall; they did not overcome them, and the palace precincts were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's ruler Jian sent Prince Bao of Le Ping, Li Song, and Zhang Cai of the palace guard to strike Shi Min and Li Nong at Kunhua Hall by night. They failed, and the inner palace erupted in chaos.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼，僞若不知者，夜斬松、才于西中華門，幷殺苞。

translations.literal: Jian was afraid and pretended not to know; that night he beheaded Song and Cai at the Western Zhonghua Gate and also killed Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Jian panicked and feigned ignorance. That night he executed Song and Cai at the Western Zhonghua Gate and killed Bao as well.

sentences.zh: 新興王祗，虎之子也，時鎮襄國，與姚弋仲、蒲洪等連兵，移檄中外，欲共誅閔、農；

translations.literal: Prince of Xinxing Zhi, a son of Hu, then held Xiangguo; he joined arms with Yao Yizhong, Pu Hong, and others, circulated a proclamation within and without, and wished together to execute Min and Nong;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhi of Xinxing, a son of Hu, held Xiangguo. He joined Yao Yizhong, Pu Hong, and others, issued a proclamation across the realm, and called for the execution of Min and Nong;

sentences.zh: 閔、農以汝陰王琨爲大都督，與張舉及侍中呼延盛帥步騎七萬分討祗等。

translations.literal: Min and Nong made Prince of Ruyang Kun Grand Commander-in-Chief, and with Zhang Ju and Palace Attendant Huyan Sheng led seventy thousand foot and horse in separate columns to campaign against Zhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Nong made Prince Kun of Ruyang Grand Commander-in-Chief and, with Zhang Ju and Palace Attendant Huyan Sheng, marched seventy thousand foot and horse in separate columns against Zhi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 中領軍石成、侍中石啓、前河東太守石輝謀誅閔、農；

translations.literal: Central Army Commander Shi Cheng, Palace Attendant Shi Qi, and former Administrator of Hedong Shi Hui plotted to execute Min and Nong;
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Commander Shi Cheng, Palace Attendant Shi Qi, and former Administrator of Hedong Shi Hui plotted to kill Min and Nong;

sentences.zh: 閔、農皆殺之。

translations.literal: Min and Nong both killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Nong killed them all.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍孫伏都、劉銖等帥羯士三千伏于胡天，亦欲誅閔、農。

translations.literal: Dragon-Flying General Sun Fudu, Liu Zhuo, and others led three thousand Jie warriors in ambush at Hutian, likewise intending to execute Min and Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Flying General Sun Fudu, Liu Zhuo, and others lay in ambush at Hutian with three thousand Jie warriors, also plotting to kill Min and Nong.

sentences.zh: 鑒在中臺，伏都帥三十餘人將升臺挾鑒以攻之。

translations.literal: Jian was in the Central Terrace; Fudu led more than thirty men about to ascend the terrace and seize Jian to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was in the Central Terrace. Fudu led more than thirty men who were about to climb the terrace, seize the emperor, and turn on Min and Nong.

sentences.zh: 鑒見伏都毀閣道，臨問其故。

translations.literal: Jian saw Fudu destroying the covered walkway and came forward to ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Fudu tear up the covered walkway, Jian came forward and asked why.

sentences.zh: 伏都曰：「李農等反，已在東掖門。

translations.literal: Fudu said, "Li Nong and others have rebelled; they are already at the Eastern Yeye Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fudu said, "Li Nong and his faction have rebelled—they are already at the Eastern Yeye Gate.

sentences.zh: 臣欲帥衛士以討之，謹先啓知。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to lead the guards to punish them and respectfully reports this beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to lead the palace guards to crush them and have come to report this first."

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「卿是功臣，好爲官陳力。

translations.literal: Jian said, "You are a meritorious servant; exert yourself well in office for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "You are a meritorious servant. Devote your strength to the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕從臺上觀，卿勿慮無報也。」

translations.literal: I shall watch from the terrace; do not worry that you will lack reward."
translations.idiomatic: I shall watch from the terrace—you need not fear going unrewarded."

sentences.zh: 于是伏都、銖帥衆攻閔、農，不克，屯于鳳陽門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fudu and Zhuo led the host to attack Min and Nong, did not overcome them, and encamped at Fengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fudu and Zhuo attacked Min and Nong but failed and drew up at Fengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 閔、農帥衆數千毀金明門而入。

translations.literal: Min and Nong led several thousand men, smashed through Jinming Gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Nong led several thousand men in, breaching Jinming Gate.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼閔之殺己，馳招閔、農，開門內之，謂曰：「孫伏都反，卿宜速討之。」

translations.literal: Jian feared Min would kill him, hurriedly summoned Min and Nong, opened the gate and admitted them, and said, "Sun Fudu has rebelled; you should promptly punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Min would kill him, Jian hastily summoned Min and Nong, opened the gates, and said, "Sun Fudu has rebelled—you must strike him down at once."

sentences.zh: 閔、農攻斬伏都等，自鳳陽至琨華，橫尸相枕，流血成渠。

translations.literal: Min and Nong attacked and beheaded Fudu and the rest; from Fengyang to Kunhua corpses lay across one another and blood formed channels.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Nong cut down Fudu and his men; from Fengyang to Kunhua the slain lay heap upon heap and blood ran in channels.

sentences.zh: 宣令內外六夷，敢稱兵仗者斬。

translations.literal: They proclaimed throughout within and without that of the Six Barbarian peoples, whoever dared bear arms would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out to the Six Barbarian peoples within and without the capital: anyone bearing arms would be executed.

sentences.zh: 胡人或斬關、或逾城而出者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Among the Hu, those who either cut through the gates or climbed over the walls to flee were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Countless Hu fled—some hacking through the gates, others scaling the walls.

sentences.zh: 閔使尚書王簡、少府王郁帥衆數千守鑒于御龍觀，懸食以給之。

translations.literal: Min sent Grand Secretaries Wang Jian and Wang Yu of the Lesser Treasury with several thousand men to guard Jian at Imperial Dragon Watchtower, hanging up food to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Min posted Grand Secretaries Wang Jian and Wang Yu with several thousand troops to hold Jian at Imperial Dragon Watchtower and hung out provisions for his sustenance.

sentences.zh: 下令城中曰：「近日孫、劉構逆，支黨伏誅，良善一無預也。

translations.literal: He issued an order in the city saying, "Recently Sun and Liu contrived rebellion; their factions have been executed by law, and the innocent have had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed to the city, "Sun and Liu recently plotted treason; their accomplices have been executed. The innocent are untouched.

sentences.zh: 今日已後，與官同心者留，不同者各任所之。

translations.literal: From this day onward, those of one mind with the court are to remain; those who are not may each go where they will.
translations.idiomatic: From this day on, those who stand with the government may stay; those who do not may go where they please.

sentences.zh: 敕城門不復相禁。」

translations.literal: He ordered that the city gates no longer be barred to one another."
translations.idiomatic: The gates were ordered open without restriction."

sentences.zh: 于是趙人百里內悉入城，胡、羯去者填門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao people within a hundred li all entered the city; Hu and Jie departing clogged the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao subjects within a hundred li flooded into the city, while Hu and Jie pouring out filled the gates.

sentences.zh: 閔知胡之不爲己用，班令內外：「趙人斬一胡首送鳳陽門者，文官進位三等，武官悉拜牙門。」

translations.literal: Min knew the Hu would not serve him and circulated an order within and without: "A Zhao person who beheads one Hu head and delivers it to Fengyang Gate—civil officials advance three ranks; military officers are all appointed Ya Gate officers."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the Hu would not serve him, Min proclaimed: "Any Zhao man who brings a Hu head to Fengyang Gate will see civil officials promoted three ranks and all military officers made gate commanders."

sentences.zh: 一日之中，斬首數萬。

translations.literal: In a single day heads cut numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day tens of thousands of heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 閔親帥趙人以誅胡、羯，無貴賤、男女、少長皆斬之，死者二十餘萬，尸諸城外，悉爲野犬豺狼所食。

translations.literal: Min personally led Zhao people to execute Hu and Jie; without regard for noble or base, male or female, young or old, all were beheaded; the dead exceeded two hundred thousand; corpses were placed outside the walls and all were eaten by wild dogs and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Min personally led Zhao troops in the slaughter of Hu and Jie—noble and humble, male and female, young and old, none spared. More than two hundred thousand died; their bodies outside the walls were devoured by wild dogs and wolves.

sentences.zh: 其屯戍四方者，閔皆以書命趙人爲將帥者誅之，或高鼻多鬚濫死者半。

translations.literal: As for those garrisoned in the four quarters, Min all by letter ordered Zhao men who were commanders to execute them; in some cases half were wrongly killed for high noses and heavy beards.
translations.idiomatic: In the garrisons across the realm Min sent orders to Zhao commanders to kill them; in some places half the victims were innocents killed merely for high noses and heavy beards.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊遣使至凉州，約張重華共擊趙。

translations.literal: Murong Jun of Yan sent envoys to Liangzhou to arrange with Zhang Chonghua a joint attack on Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun of Yan sent envoys to Liangzhou to propose a joint strike against Zhao with Zhang Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 高句麗王釗送前東夷護軍宋晃于燕，燕王俊赦之，更名曰活，拜爲中尉。

translations.literal: King Chao of Goguryeo sent the former Protector of the East Barbarians Song Huang to Yan; Murong Jun pardoned him, changed his name to Huo, and appointed him Central Captain.
translations.idiomatic: King Chao of Goguryeo delivered former Protector of the East Barbarians Song Huang to Yan. Murong Jun pardoned him, renamed him Huo, and made him Central Captain.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，趙大將軍閔欲滅去石氏之迹，托以讖文有「繼趙李」，更國號曰衛，易姓李氏，大赦，改元青龍。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Grand General of Zhao Min wished to efface the traces of the Shi clan; citing a prophecy-text reading "succeed Zhao—Li," he changed the state name to Wei, altered his surname to Li, granted a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Qinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhao's Grand General Min sought to erase every trace of the Shi. Citing a prophecy that read "After Zhao comes Li," he renamed the state Wei, took the surname Li, declared a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Qinglong.

sentences.zh: 太宰趙庶、太尉張舉、中軍將軍張春、光祿大夫石岳、撫軍石寧、武衛將軍張季及公侯、卿、校、龍騰等萬餘人，出奔襄國，汝陰王琨奔冀州。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zhao Shu, Grand Marshal Zhang Ju, Central Army General Zhang Chun, Household Grandee Shi Yue, Pacification General Shi Ning, Guards General Zhang Ji, and more than ten thousand among nobles, ministers, colonels, and Dragon Soarers fled to Xiangguo; Prince of Ruyang Kun fled to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Zhao Shu, Grand Marshal Zhang Ju, Central Army General Zhang Chun, Household Grandee Shi Yue, Pacification General Shi Ning, Guards General Zhang Ji, and more than ten thousand nobles, ministers, colonels, and Dragon Soarers fled to Xiangguo. Prince Kun of Ruyang fled to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍張沈據滏口，張賀度據石瀆，建義將軍段勤據黎陽，寧南將軍楊群據桑壁，劉國據陽城，段龕據陳留，姚弋仲據灄頭，蒲洪據枋頭，衆各數萬，皆不附于閔。

translations.literal: Pacification General Zhang Shen held Fucou, Zhang Hedou held Shidu, Establishing Righteousness General Duan Qin held Liyang, Pacifying South General Yang Qun held Sangbi, Liu Guo held Yangcheng, Duan Kan held Chenliu, Yao Yizhong held Tantou, Pu Hong held Fangtou—each had tens of thousands of followers and none submitted to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification General Zhang Shen held Fucou; Zhang Hedou, Shidu; Duan Qin, Liyang; Yang Qun, Sangbi; Liu Guo, Yangcheng; Duan Kan, Chenliu; Yao Yizhong, Tantou; Pu Hong, Fangtou—each commanded tens of thousands and none submitted to Min.

sentences.zh: 勤，末柸之子；

translations.literal: Qin was a son of Mo Ti;
translations.idiomatic: Qin was a son of Mo Ti;

sentences.zh: 龕，蘭之子也。

translations.literal: Kan was a son of Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was a son of Lan.

sentences.zh: 王朗、麻秋自長安赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu went from Chang'an toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu marched from Chang'an toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋承閔書，誅朗部胡千餘人。

translations.literal: Qiu received Min's letter and executed more than a thousand Hu in Lang's division.
translations.idiomatic: On Min's orders, Qiu executed more than a thousand Hu in Lang's command.

sentences.zh: 朗奔襄國。

translations.literal: Lang fled to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Lang fled to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 秋帥衆歸鄴，蒲洪使其子龍驤將軍雄迎擊，獲之，以爲軍師將軍。

translations.literal: Qiu led the host back to Ye; Pu Hong sent his son Dragon-Flying General Xiong to meet and strike him, captured him, and made him Strategist General.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu marched back to Ye. Pu Hong sent his son, Dragon-Flying General Xiong, to intercept him. Xiong captured Qiu and appointed him Strategist General.

sentences.zh: 汝陰王琨及張舉、王朗帥衆七萬伐鄴，大將軍閔帥騎千餘與戰于城北；

translations.literal: Prince of Ruyang Kun together with Zhang Ju and Wang Lang led seventy thousand to attack Ye; Grand General Min led more than a thousand horsemen and fought them north of the city;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kun of Ruyang, Zhang Ju, and Wang Lang marched seventy thousand against Ye. Grand General Min met them north of the city with just over a thousand cavalry;

sentences.zh: 閔操兩刃矛，馳騎擊之，所向摧陷，斬首三千級，琨等大敗而去。

translations.literal: Min wielded a double-edged spear, charged on horseback to strike them, and wherever he advanced they were shattered; he cut off three thousand heads, and Kun and the rest were utterly defeated and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wielding a double-edged spear, Min charged. Wherever he rode the enemy line collapsed. Three thousand heads fell; Kun and the rest fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 閔與李農帥騎三萬討張賀度于石瀆。

translations.literal: Min and Li Nong led thirty thousand horsemen to campaign against Zhang Hedou at Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: Min and Li Nong led thirty thousand cavalry against Zhang Hedou at Shidu.

sentences.zh: 閏月，衛主鑒密遣宦者賫書召張沈等，使乘虛襲鄴。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, the ruler of Wei Jian secretly sent eunuchs bearing letters to summon Zhang Shen and the rest to take advantage of the moment and strike Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Wei ruler Jian secretly sent eunuchs with letters summoning Zhang Shen and others to strike Ye while it was undefended.

sentences.zh: 宦者以告閔、農，閔、農馳還，廢鑒，殺之，幷殺趙主虎三十八孫，盡滅石氏，姚弋仲子曜武將軍益、武衛將軍若帥禁兵數千斬關奔灄頭。

translations.literal: A eunuch reported this to Min and Nong; Min and Nong galloped back, deposed Jian, and killed him; they also killed the thirty-eight grandsons of Zhao ruler Hu and utterly exterminated the Shi clan; Yao Yizhong's sons, Lightning Martial General Yi and Guards General Ruo, led several thousand forbidden troops, cut through the gate, and fled to Tantou.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch betrayed the plot to Min and Nong. They galloped back, deposed Jian, and killed him along with all thirty-eight grandsons of Hu—wiping out the Shi line. Yao Yizhong's sons Yi and Ruo led several thousand palace guards through the gates and fled to Tantou.

sentences.zh: 弋仲帥衆討閔，軍于混轎。

translations.literal: Yizhong led forces to campaign against Min and encamped at Hunjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong marched against Min and encamped at Hunjiao.

sentences.zh: 司徒申鐘等上尊號于閔，閔以讓李農，農固辭。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Shen Zhong and others offered the exalted title to Min; Min yielded it to Li Nong, and Nong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Shen Zhong and others offered Min the imperial title. Min tried to yield it to Li Nong, who firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 閔曰：「吾屬故晋人也，今晋室猶存，請與諸君分割州郡，各稱牧、守、公、侯，奉表迎晋天子還都洛陽，何如？」

translations.literal: Min said, "Our company are originally men of Jin; now the Jin house still exists—let us partition the provinces and commanderies, each take the title of governor, defender, duke, or marquis, and present a memorial to welcome the Jin Son of Heaven back to the capital at Luoyang—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "We were Jin subjects once. The Jin house endures. Let us divide the realm—each take governor or marquis—and submit a petition to welcome the Jin emperor home to Luoyang. What say you?"

sentences.zh: 尚書胡睦進曰：「陛下聖德應天，宜登在位，晋氏衰微，遠竄江表，豈能總馭英雄，混壹四海乎！」

translations.literal: Chief of the Secretariat Hu Mu advanced and said, "Your Majesty's sage virtue answers Heaven; you ought to ascend the throne. The Jin clan has declined and fled far to the lands south of the river—how could they marshal the heroes and unify the Four Seas?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief of the Secretariat Hu Mu stepped forward: "Your Majesty's virtue answers Heaven—you must take the throne. The Jin are spent, driven south of the Yangzi. How could they command heroes or unite the realm?"

sentences.zh: 閔曰：「胡尚書之言，可謂識機知命矣。」

translations.literal: Min said, "Minister Hu's words may be called knowing the moment and recognizing destiny."
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "Minister Hu knows the moment and his place in it."

sentences.zh: 乃即皇帝位，大赦，改元永興，國號大魏。

translations.literal: He thereupon assumed the emperor's throne, granted a general amnesty, changed the era name to Yongxing, and declared the state name Great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took the throne, declared an amnesty, adopted the era name Yongxing, and named the state Great Wei.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞中原大亂，復謀進取。

translations.literal: The court heard that the Central Plains were in great turmoil and again plotted a forward advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of chaos across the Central Plains, the Jin court again planned a northern advance.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以揚州刺史殷浩爲中軍將軍、假節、都督揚、豫、徐、兗、青五州諸軍事，以蒲洪爲氐王、使持節、征北大將軍、都督河北諸軍事、冀州剌史、廣川郡公；

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Inspector of Yangzhou Yin Hao was made Central Army General, Acting with Full Powers, and overseer of military affairs in Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, and Qing; Pu Hong was made King of the Di, Bearer of the Staff with credentials, Northern Expedition Grand General, overseer of military affairs in Hebei, Inspector of Jizhou, and Duke of Guangchuan;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou Yin Hao, Inspector of Yangzhou, was made Central Army General with acting full powers and commander of five provinces. Pu Hong was named King of the Di, granted the staff of authority, made Northern Expedition Grand General and Inspector of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Guangchuan;

sentences.zh: 蒲健爲假節、右將軍、監河北征討前鋒諸軍事、襄國公。

translations.literal: Pu Jian was made Acting with Full Powers, Right General, overseer of the forward vanguard forces campaigning in Hebei, and Duke of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Jian was made Right General with acting full powers and commander of the Hebei vanguard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲、蒲洪各有據關右之志。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong and Pu Hong each harbored the ambition to hold the Pass and the west.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong and Pu Hong each intended to seize the northwest.

sentences.zh: 弋仲遣其子襄帥衆五萬擊洪，洪迎擊，破之，斬獲三萬餘級。

translations.literal: Yizhong sent his son Xiang to lead fifty thousand to strike Hong; Hong met the attack and defeated them, slaying and capturing more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong sent his son Xiang with fifty thousand to attack Hong. Hong met them, won a crushing victory, and took more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 洪自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、三秦王，改姓苻氏。

translations.literal: Hong styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of the Three Qin, and changed his surname to the Fu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hong proclaimed himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and King of the Three Qin, and adopted the surname Fu.

sentences.zh: 以南安雷弱兒爲輔國將軍；

translations.literal: He made Lei Ruo'er of Nan'an Assistant State General;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Lei Ruo'er of Nan'an Assistant State General;

sentences.zh: 安定梁欏爲前將軍，領左長史；

translations.literal: Liang Luo of Anding was made Forward General and held the post of Left Chief Clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Luo of Anding Forward General and Left Chief Clerk;

sentences.zh: 馮翊魚遵爲右將軍，領右長史；

translations.literal: Yu Zun of Fengyi was made Right General and held the post of Right Chief Clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zun of Fengyi Right General and Right Chief Clerk;

sentences.zh: 京兆段陵爲左將軍，領左司馬；

translations.literal: Duan Ling of Jingzhao was made Left General and held the post of Left Major;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ling of Jingzhao Left General and Left Major;

sentences.zh: 王墮爲右將軍，領右司馬；

translations.literal: Wang Duo was made Right General and held the post of Right Major;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo Right General and Right Major;

sentences.zh: 天水趙俱、隴西牛夷、北地辛牢皆爲從事中郎；

translations.literal: Zhao Ju of Tianshui, Niu Yi of Longxi, and Xin Lao of Beidi were all made Attendant Gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ju of Tianshui, Niu Yi of Longxi, and Xin Lao of Beidi were all made Attendant Gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 氐酋毛貴爲單于輔相。

translations.literal: the Di chieftain Mao Gui was made Chanyu Assistant Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: the Di chieftain Mao Gui Chanyu Assistant Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 二月，燕王俊使慕容霸將兵二萬自東道出徒河，慕輿于自西道出蠮螉塞，俊自中道出盧龍塞，以伐趙。

translations.literal: In the second month, Murong Jun of Yan sent Murong Ba to lead twenty thousand troops by the eastern route out through Tuhe, Muyu Yu by the western route out through Xiemei Pass, and Jun himself by the central route out through Lulong Pass to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Murong Jun sent Murong Ba with twenty thousand men east through Tuhe, Muyu Yu west through Xiemei Pass, and himself through Lulong Pass in the center—all marching against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以慕容恪、鮮于亮爲前驅，命慕輿泥槎山通道。

translations.literal: He made Murong Ke and Xianyu Liang the vanguard and ordered Muyu Ni to open a passage through the mountains with rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke and Xianyu Liang led the van; Muyu Ni was ordered to cut a mountain road.

sentences.zh: 留世子曄守龍城，以內史劉斌爲大司農，與典書令皇甫真留統後事。

translations.literal: He left the heir apparent Ye to guard Longcheng, made Internal Administrator Liu Bin Grand Minister of Agriculture, and left him with Master of Documents Huangfu Zhen to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Ye remained at Longcheng; Internal Administrator Liu Bin was made Grand Minister of Agriculture and, with Master of Documents Huangfu Zhen, left to govern the rear.

sentences.zh: 霸軍至三陘，趙征東將軍鄧恒惶怖，焚倉庫，弃安樂遁去，與幽州刺史王午共保薊。

translations.literal: Ba's army reached Sanshen; Zhao's Eastern Campaign General Deng Heng was terrified, burned the storehouses, abandoned Anle and fled, and together with Inspector of Youzhou Wang Wu held Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ba reached Sanshen. Zhao's Eastern Campaign General Deng Heng panicked, torched the granaries, abandoned Anle, and fled to Ji with Inspector of Youzhou Wang Wu.

sentences.zh: 徙河南部都尉孫泳急入安樂，撲滅餘火，籍其穀帛。

translations.literal: He transferred Commandant of Henan Interior Sun Yong to hurry into Anle, beat out the remaining fires, and register its grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commandant of Henan Interior Sun Yong into Anle at once to extinguish the fires and inventory the grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 霸收安樂、北平兵糧，與俊會臨渠。

translations.literal: Ba gathered the military grain of Anle and Beiping and joined Jun at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Ba collected the stores of Anle and Beiping and joined Jun at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 三月，燕兵至無終。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yan troops reached Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Yan army reached Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 王午留其將王佗以數千人守薊，與鄧恒走保魯口。

translations.literal: Wang Wu left his general Wang Tuo with several thousand men to hold Ji and fled with Deng Heng to secure Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu left general Wang Tuo with several thousand men at Ji and withdrew with Deng Heng to Lukou.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，俊拔薊，執王佗，斬之。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Jun took Ji, seized Wang Tuo, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi Jun took Ji, seized Wang Tuo, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 俊欲悉坑其士卒千餘人，慕容霸諫曰：「趙爲暴虐，王興師伐之，將以拯民于塗炭而撫有中州也；

translations.literal: Jun wished to bury alive all more than a thousand of their soldiers; Murong Ba remonstrated, saying, "Zhao has been cruel and tyrannical; Your Majesty raised troops to punish them in order to rescue the people from fire and water and pacify the Central Plains;
translations.idiomatic: Jun meant to bury alive the thousand-odd defenders. Murong Ba remonstrated: "Zhao ruled with cruelty. Your Majesty marched to rescue the people from misery and pacify the Central Plains;

sentences.zh: 今始得薊而坑其士卒，恐不可以爲王師之先聲也。」

translations.literal: now, having just taken Ji, to bury their soldiers alive— I fear this cannot serve as the first report of a royal army."
translations.idiomatic: to massacre them the moment we take Ji would be a poor first note for a royal campaign."

sentences.zh: 乃釋之。

translations.literal: He thereupon released them.
translations.idiomatic: He spared them.

sentences.zh: 俊入都于薊，中州士女降者相繼。

translations.literal: Jun entered and made Ji his capital; men and women of the Central Plains submitting followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Ji his capital, and Central Plains families surrendered in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至范陽，范陽太守李産欲爲石氏拒燕，衆莫爲用，乃帥八城令長出降；

translations.literal: Yan troops reached Fanyang; Administrator of Fanyang Li Chan wished to resist Yan on behalf of the Shi clan, but none would follow him, so he led the magistrates of eight cities out to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: At Fanyang, Administrator Li Chan tried to hold the city for the Shi, but none would follow. He led the magistrates of eight districts out to surrender;

sentences.zh: 俊復以産爲太守。

translations.literal: Jun again made Chan administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reappointed him administrator.

sentences.zh: 産子績爲幽州別駕，弃其家從王午在魯口。

translations.literal: Chan's son Ji was Aide of Youzhou; he abandoned his family and followed Wang Wu at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: Chan's son Ji, Aide of Youzhou, had abandoned his family to follow Wang Wu at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 鄧恒謂午曰：「績鄉里在北，父已降燕，今雖在此，恐終難相保，徒爲人累，不如去之。」

translations.literal: Deng Heng said to Wu, "Ji's home district is in the north; his father has already surrendered to Yan. Though he is here now, I fear in the end he will be hard to keep in trust and will only be a burden on others—better to remove him."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Heng told Wu, "Ji's home is in the north and his father has surrendered to Yan. He cannot be trusted here—he is only a liability. Better to send him away."

sentences.zh: 午曰：「此何言也！

translations.literal: Wu said, "What words are these!
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, "What kind of talk is that!

sentences.zh: 夫以當今喪亂，而績乃能立義捐家，情節之重，雖古烈士無以過，乃欲以猜嫌害之？

translations.literal: In this age of ruin and disorder, that Ji could establish righteousness and abandon his family—the weight of his integrity, though ancient martyrs could not surpass it—and you would harm him out of suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: In these times of chaos he chose loyalty over family—a devotion ancient martyrs could not exceed—and you would kill him on suspicion?

sentences.zh: 燕、趙之士聞之，謂我直相聚爲賊，了無意識。

translations.literal: When men of Yan and Zhao hear of it, they will say we have simply gathered to be bandits, utterly without principle.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Yan and Zhao will say we are nothing but bandits who have lost all sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 衆情一散，不可復集，此爲坐自屠潰也。」

translations.literal: Once the host's hearts scatter, they cannot be gathered again—this is to sit and slaughter and rout oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Once morale breaks it cannot be restored—we would be destroying ourselves."

sentences.zh: 恒乃止。

translations.literal: Heng thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Heng desisted.

sentences.zh: 午猶慮諸將不與己同心，或致非意，乃遣績歸。

translations.literal: Wu still feared the generals were not of one mind with him and might do him harm, so he sent Ji back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu still feared his generals might turn on him and sent Ji away.

sentences.zh: 績始辭午往見燕王俊，俊讓之曰：「卿不識天命，弃父邀名，今日乃始來邪！」

translations.literal: Ji for the first time took leave of Wu and went to see Murong Jun of Yan; Jun reproached him, saying, "You did not recognize Heaven's mandate, abandoned your father to seek fame—only today do you come?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji left Wu and went to Murong Jun. Jun reproached him: "You defied Heaven's mandate, abandoned your father for reputation—only now do you come?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣眷戀舊主，志存微節，官身所在，何事非君！

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant was attached to his former lord and kept a modest integrity in mind; wherever one's office and person are stationed, what affair is not that of one's lord!
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I was bound to my former lord and held to a small integrity. Where one's office lies, that is one's sovereign!

sentences.zh: 殿下方以義取天下，臣未謂得見之晚也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness is just now taking the realm by righteousness; your servant does not consider it late to be received."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness wins the realm by righteousness. I do not consider myself late."

sentences.zh: 俊悅，善待之。

translations.literal: Jun was pleased and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was pleased and treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 俊以弟宜爲代郡城郎，孫泳爲廣寧太守，悉置幽州郡縣守宰。

translations.literal: Jun made his younger brother Yi commandant of Dai commandery, Sun Yong Administrator of Guangning, and fully appointed defenders and magistrates for Youzhou's commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made his brother Yi commandant of Dai, Sun Yong administrator of Guangning, and installed officials throughout Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，俊使中部俟厘慕輿句督薊中留事，自將擊鄧恒于魯口。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Jun sent Central Tribal Attendant Muyu Gou to oversee affairs left at Ji and personally led troops to strike Deng Heng at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi Jun left Muyu Gou to govern Ji and marched in person against Deng Heng at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 軍至清梁，恒將鹿勃早將數千人夜襲燕營，半已得入，先犯前鋒都督慕容霸，突入幕下，霸起奮擊，手殺十餘人，早不能進。

translations.literal: When the army reached Qingliang, Heng's general Lu Boao led several thousand men in a night raid on the Yan camp; half had already entered; they first struck Vanguard Commander Murong Ba, burst into his tent, Ba rose and fought fiercely, personally killing more than ten men, and Boao could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingliang, Heng's general Lu Boao led several thousand in a night raid. Half the raiders were already inside when they struck Vanguard Commander Murong Ba in his tent. Ba leapt up and killed more than ten with his own hand; Boao could not press forward.

sentences.zh: 由是燕軍得嚴，俊謂慕輿根曰：「賊鋒甚銳，宜且避之。」

translations.literal: Thereby the Yan army was brought to order; Jun said to Muyu Gen, "The enemy's edge is very sharp; we ought for the moment to avoid them."
translations.idiomatic: The Yan camp rallied. Jun told Muyu Gen, "The enemy is fierce—we should pull back for now."

sentences.zh: 根正色曰：「我衆彼寡，力不相敵，故乘夜來戰，冀萬一獲利。

translations.literal: Gen said with a stern face, "We are many and they few; in strength we do not match them, so they came by night to fight, hoping for one chance in ten thousand of gain.
translations.idiomatic: Gen said sternly, "They are few and we are many—that is why they struck at night, gambling on surprise.

sentences.zh: 今求賊得賊，正當擊之，復何所疑！

translations.literal: Now that we have sought the enemy and found the enemy, we should just strike them—what is there to doubt!
translations.idiomatic: We have found them—strike! What is there to hesitate over?

sentences.zh: 王但安臥，臣等自爲王破之！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only lie at ease; your servants will break them for Your Majesty themselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only rest—we will break them for you!"

sentences.zh: 俊不能自安，內史李洪從俊出營外，屯高冢上。

translations.literal: Jun could not be at ease; Internal Administrator Li Hong followed Jun out of the camp and encamped on a high mound.
translations.idiomatic: Jun could not settle. Internal Administrator Li Hong escorted him outside the camp to a high mound.

sentences.zh: 根帥左右精勇數百人從中牙直前擊早，李洪徐整騎隊還助之，早乃退走。

translations.literal: Gen led several hundred picked brave men at his left and right straight from the central standard to strike Boao; Li Hong slowly arrayed the cavalry squadrons and returned to assist; Boao then retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gen led several hundred picked warriors straight at Boao from the center; Li Hong wheeled the cavalry squadrons back to help; Boao fled.

sentences.zh: 衆軍追擊四十餘里，早僅以身免，所從士卒死亡略盡。

translations.literal: The host pursued for more than forty li; Boao barely escaped with his person; the soldiers who followed him were nearly all dead.
translations.idiomatic: The army pursued more than forty li. Boao escaped with his life alone; his men were nearly all killed.

sentences.zh: 俊引兵還薊。

translations.literal: Jun led the troops back to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jun withdrew to Ji.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔復姓冉氏，尊母王氏爲皇太后，立妻董氏爲皇后，子智爲皇太子，胤、明裕皆爲王。

translations.literal: Wei ruler Min restored the surname Ran; he honored his mother Lady Wang as Empress Dowager, installed his wife the Lady Dong as Empress, made his son Zhi Crown Prince, and made Yin and Mingyu both princes.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Min restored the Ran surname, honored his mother Lady Wang as Empress Dowager, made his wife Lady Dong empress, his son Zhi crown prince, and Yin and Mingyu princes.

sentences.zh: 以李農爲太宰、領太尉、錄尚書事，封齊王，其子皆封縣公。

translations.literal: He made Li Nong Grand Tutor, concurrently Grand Marshal, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and enfeoffed all his sons as county marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong was made Grand Tutor and Grand Marshal with charge of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi; his sons were all made county marquises.

sentences.zh: 遣使者持節赦諸軍屯，皆不從。

translations.literal: He sent envoys bearing the staff to grant amnesty to the various army garrisons; none obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with the staff of authority to offer amnesty to the garrisons; none accepted.

sentences.zh: 麻秋說苻洪曰：「冉閔、石祗方相持，中原之亂未可平也。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu urged Fu Hong, saying, "Ran Min and Shi Zhi are just now locked in stalemate; the turmoil of the Central Plains cannot yet be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu urged Fu Hong: "Ran Min and Shi Zhi are locked in stalemate. The Central Plains cannot be pacified yet.

sentences.zh: 不如先取關中，基業已固，然後東爭天下，誰能敵之！」

translations.literal: It would be better first to take Guanzhong; once the foundation is firm, then contend for the realm in the east—who could oppose you!"
translations.idiomatic: Better seize Guanzhong first. With a firm base, then contest the east—who could stand against you?"

sentences.zh: 洪深然之。

translations.literal: Hong deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Hong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而秋因宴鴆洪，欲幷其衆；

translations.literal: Before long Qiu, taking advantage of a banquet, poisoned Hong and wished to absorb his forces;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qiu poisoned Hong at a feast, intending to absorb his troops;

sentences.zh: 世子健收秋斬之。

translations.literal: Heir Jian seized Qiu and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jian arrested Qiu and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 洪謂健曰：「吾所以未入關者，以爲中州可定；

translations.literal: Hong told Jian, "The reason I have not entered the Pass is that I thought the Central Plains could be settled;
translations.idiomatic: Hong told Jian, "I stayed out of the Pass because I thought we could secure the Central Plains;

sentences.zh: 今不幸爲竪子所困。

translations.literal: Now, unhappily, I am trapped by that wretched fellow.
translations.idiomatic: Now that scoundrel has trapped me.

sentences.zh: 中州非汝兄弟所能辦，我死，汝急入關！」

translations.literal: The Central Plains is not something you brothers can accomplish; when I die, hurry into the Pass!"
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains is beyond you and your brothers. When I die, march into the Pass at once!"

sentences.zh: 言終而卒。

translations.literal: With these words finished, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke no more and died.

sentences.zh: 健代統其衆，乃去大都督、大將軍、三秦王之號，稱晋官爵，遣其叔父安來告喪，且請朝命。

translations.literal: Jian succeeded to command of the host; he then discarded the titles Grand Commander, Grand General, and Prince of Three Qins, adopted Jin offices and ranks, and sent his uncle Fu An to announce the death and also request imperial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Jian took command, shed the titles of Grand Commander, Grand General, and Prince of Three Qins, assumed Jin offices, and sent his uncle Fu An to report the death and seek court confirmation.

sentences.zh: 趙新興王祗即皇帝位于襄國，改元永守。

translations.literal: Zhao's Prince of Xinxing Zhi took the imperial throne at Xiangguo and changed the era name to Yongshou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhi of Xinxing declared himself emperor at Xiangguo and adopted the era name Yongshou.

sentences.zh: 以汝陰王琨爲相國，六夷據州郡擁兵者皆應之。

translations.literal: He made Prince of Ruyin Kun Chancellor of State; all the six barbarian groups holding provinces and commanderies with armed forces answered his call.
translations.idiomatic: He named Prince Kun of Ruyin chancellor of state; every tribal warlord holding a province answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 祗以姚弋仲爲右丞相、親趙王，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Zhi made Yao Yizhong Right Chancellor and Prince who Honors Zhao, treating him with extraordinary ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi made Yao Yizhong right chancellor and Prince Who Honors Zhao, honoring him with exceptional ceremony.

sentences.zh: 弋仲子襄，雄勇多才略，士民愛之，請弋仲以爲嗣，弋仲以襄非長子，不許；

translations.literal: Yizhong's son Xiang was bold and brave, with many stratagems; gentry and commoners loved him and asked Yizhong to make him heir; Yizhong, because Xiang was not the eldest son, did not consent;
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong's son Xiang was bold and gifted; the people loved him and begged Yizhong to name him heir. Yizhong refused because Xiang was not the eldest son;

sentences.zh: 請者日以千數，弋仲乃使之將兵。

translations.literal: petitioners came by the thousands daily; Yizhong then had him command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands petitioned each day until Yizhong finally gave him a command.

sentences.zh: 祗以襄爲驃騎將軍、豫州刺史、新昌公。

translations.literal: Zhi made Xiang Rapid Cavalry General, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi named Xiang Rapid Cavalry General, inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 又以苻健爲都督河南諸軍事、鎮南大將軍、開府儀同三司，兗州牧、略陽郡公。

translations.literal: He also made Fu Jian commander of all military affairs south of the River, Pacifying South Grand General, with staff equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Yanzhou, and Duke of Lueyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was made commander of Henan armies, Pacifying South Grand General with staff equal to the Three Excellencies, governor of Yanzhou, and Duke of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，趙主祗遣汝陰王琨將兵十萬伐魏。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhao ruler Zhi sent Prince of Ruyin Kun with one hundred thousand troops to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhao ruler Zhi sent Prince Kun of Ruyin with a hundred thousand men against Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔殺李農及其三子，幷尚書令王謨、侍中王衍、中常待嚴震、趙升。

translations.literal: Wei ruler Min killed Li Nong and his three sons, together with Masters of Writing Wang Mo, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan, Regular Attendant Yan Zhen, and Zhao Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Min executed Li Nong and his three sons, along with Wang Mo, Wang Yan, Yan Zhen, and Zhao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 閔遣使臨江告晋曰：「逆胡亂中原，今已誅之；

translations.literal: Min sent an envoy to the riverfront to inform Jin, saying, "The rebellious barbarians threw the Central Plains into chaos; they have now been executed;
translations.idiomatic: Min sent envoys to the Yangzi to tell Jin: "The barbarian rebels ravaged the Central Plains. We have destroyed them;

sentences.zh: 能共討者，可遣軍來也」。

translations.literal: those who can join in the punitive campaign may send troops."
translations.idiomatic: any who will join the campaign may send armies."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不應。

translations.literal: The court gave no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court ignored the offer.

sentences.zh: 五月，廬江太守袁真攻魏合肥，克之，虜其居民而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Lujiang Administrator Yuan Zhen attacked Wei's Hefei, took it, carried off the inhabitants, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Lujiang administrator Yuan Zhen took Hefei from Wei, deported the population, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六月，趙汝陰王琨進據邯鄲，鎮南將軍劉國自繁陽會之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhao's Prince of Ruyin Kun advanced and held Handan; Pacifying South General Liu Guo joined him from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Prince Kun of Ruyin seized Handan while Pacifying South General Liu Guo marched from Fanyang to join him.

sentences.zh: 魏衛將軍王泰擊琨，大破之，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Wei's Guard General Wang Tai attacked Kun and utterly defeated him; more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Wei guard general Wang Tai shattered Kun's army, killing more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 劉國還繁陽。

translations.literal: Liu Guo returned to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guo withdrew to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 初，段蘭卒于令支，段龕代領其衆，因石氏之亂，擁部落南徙。

translations.literal: Earlier, Duan Lan had died at Lingzhi; Duan Kan succeeded to command of his host; taking advantage of the chaos of the Shi clan, he led his tribes southward.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lan had died at Lingzhi, and Kan succeeded him. Exploiting the Shi collapse, Kan led his tribes south.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，龕引兵東據廣固，自稱齊王。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Kan led troops east, seized Guanggu, and styled himself King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Kan marched east, seized Guanggu, and declared himself King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 八月，代郡人趙榼帥三百餘家叛燕，歸趙幷州刺史張平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhao Ke of Dai Commandery led more than three hundred households in revolt against Yan and surrendered to Zhao's Inspector of Bingzhou Zhang Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhao Ke of Dai commandery led three hundred-odd households in revolt against Yan to join Zhao inspector Zhang Ping.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊徙廣寧、上穀二郡民于徐無，代郡民于凡城。

translations.literal: Yan's Jun relocated the people of Guangning and Shanggu commanderies to Xuwu, and the people of Dai Commandery to Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun resettled Guangning and Shanggu to Xuwu and moved Dai commandery's people to Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 王朗之去長安也，朗司馬京兆杜洪據長安，自稱晋征北將軍、雍州刺史，以馮翊張琚爲司馬；

translations.literal: When Wang Lang left Chang'an, Lang's Registrar from Jingzhao, Du Hong, held Chang'an, styled himself Jin's Campaign North General and Inspector of Yongzhou, and made Zhang Ju of Fufeng his registrar;
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lang abandoned Chang'an, his registrar Du Hong of Jingzhao seized the city, styled himself Jin campaign north general and inspector of Yong, and made Zhang Ju of Fufeng his registrar;

sentences.zh: 關西夷、夏皆應之。

translations.literal: all the barbarians and Chinese of the west answered him.
translations.idiomatic: barbarians and Chinese across the west rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 苻健欲取之，恐洪知之，乃受趙官爵。

translations.literal: Fu Jian wished to take it but feared Hong would learn of this; he therefore accepted Zhao offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian meant to seize the region but feared tipping his hand; he accepted Zhao titles as cover.

sentences.zh: 以趙俱爲河內太守，戍溫；

translations.literal: He made Zhao Ju Administrator of Henei, garrisoning Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ju he made governor of Henei, garrisoning Wen;

sentences.zh: 牛夷爲安集將軍，戍懷；

translations.literal: Niu Yi Pacifying Settlements General, garrisoning Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yi pacifying settlements general, garrisoning Huai;

sentences.zh: 治宮室于枋頭，課民種麥，示無西意，有知而不種者，健殺之以徇。

translations.literal: he built palaces at Fangtou, set the people to planting wheat, showing no intention to go west; those who knew but would not plant—Jian killed them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: at Fangtou he built palaces and set the people to plant wheat, feigning no move west. Anyone who understood the ruse and refused to plant was executed as an example.

sentences.zh: 既而自稱晋征西大將軍、都督關中諸軍事、雍州刺史；

translations.literal: Then he styled himself Jin's Campaign West Grand General, commander of all military affairs in Guanzhong, and Inspector of Yongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Then he took Jin titles—campaign west grand general, commander of Guanzhong, inspector of Yong—

sentences.zh: 以武威賈玄碩爲左長史，洛陽梁安爲長史，段純爲左司馬，辛牢爲右司馬，京兆王魚、安定程肱、胡文等爲軍咨祭酒，悉衆而西。

translations.literal: he made Jia Xuanshuo of Wuwei Left Chief Clerk, Liang An of Luoyang Chief Clerk, Duan Chun Left Commander, Xin Lao Right Commander, and Wang Yu of Jingzhao, Cheng Gong of Anding, Hu Wen, and others Army Advisers; and led the whole host westward.
translations.idiomatic: and named Jia Xuanshuo, Liang An, Duan Chun, Xin Lao, Wang Yu, Cheng Gong, and Hu Wen to staff posts before marching west with his whole army.

sentences.zh: 以魚遵爲前鋒，行至盟津，爲浮梁以濟。

translations.literal: He made Yu Zun vanguard; reaching Mengjin, they built a pontoon bridge to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zun led the van; at Mengjin they threw a pontoon bridge across the river.

sentences.zh: 遣弟輔國將軍雄帥衆五千自潼關入，兄子揚武將軍菁帥衆七千自軹關入。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother, Supporting the State General Xiong, to lead five thousand troops in through Tong Pass, and his brother's son, Martial Splendor General Jing, seven thousand in through Zhi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xiong led five thousand through Tong Pass; his nephew Jing, seven thousand through Zhi Pass.

sentences.zh: 臨別，執菁手曰：「若事不捷，汝死河北，我死河南，不復相見。」

translations.literal: At parting he took Jing's hand and said, "If matters do not succeed, you die north of the River, I die south of the River—we shall not meet again."
translations.idiomatic: Taking Jing's hand at parting he said, "If we fail, you die north of the river and I south—we shall not meet again.

sentences.zh: 既濟，焚橋，自帥大衆隨雄而進。

translations.literal: Once across, they burned the bridge; he himself led the main force following Xiong forward.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, they burned the bridge. Jian led the main column after Xiong.

sentences.zh: 杜洪聞之，與健書，侮嫚之。

translations.literal: When Du Hong heard this, he wrote to Jian, insulting and reviling him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong answered Jian's advance with letters of abuse.

sentences.zh: 以張琚弟先爲征虜將軍，帥衆萬三千逆戰于潼關之北。

translations.literal: He made Zhang Ju's younger brother Xian Campaign General Who Subdues Barbarians, to lead thirteen thousand troops to give battle north of Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Ju's brother Xian with thirteen thousand men to meet them north of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 先兵大敗，走還長安。

translations.literal: Xian's army was utterly defeated and fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was routed and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 洪悉召關中之衆以拒健。

translations.literal: Hong summoned all forces in Guanzhong to resist Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Hong called up every force in Guanzhong to block Jian.

sentences.zh: 洪弟郁勸洪迎健，洪不從；

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Yu urged Hong to welcome Jian; Hong would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Yu urged him to welcome Jian. Hong refused;

sentences.zh: 郁帥所部降于健。

translations.literal: Yu led his division in surrender to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu brought his division over to Jian.

sentences.zh: 健遣苻雄徇渭北。

translations.literal: Jian sent Fu Xiong to sweep north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sent Fu Xiong north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 氐酋毛受屯高陵，徐磋屯好畤，羌酋白犢屯黃白，衆各數萬，皆斬洪使，遣子降于健。

translations.literal: Di chief Mao Shou camped at Gaoling, Xu Cuo at Haozhi, Qiang chief Bai Du at Huangbai—each had tens of thousands; all killed Hong's envoys, sent sons to surrender to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Di chief Mao Shou held Gaoling, Xu Cuo Haozhi, Qiang chief Bai Du Huangbai—each commanded tens of thousands, killed Hong's envoys, and sent sons to surrender.

sentences.zh: 苻菁、魚遵所過城邑，無不降附。

translations.literal: Every city-town that Fu Jing and Yu Zun passed submitted without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Every town Jing and Yu Zun passed submitted.

sentences.zh: 洪懼，固守長安。

translations.literal: Hong was afraid and held fast within Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hong locked himself in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 張賀度、段勤、劉國、靳豚會于昌城，將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Zhang Hedou, Duan Qin, Liu Guo, and Jin Tun met at Changcheng, intending to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedou, Duan Qin, Liu Guo, and Jin Tun united at Changcheng to march on Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔自將擊之，戰于蒼亭，賀度等大敗，死者二萬八千人，追斬靳豚于陰安，盡俘其衆而歸。

translations.literal: Wei ruler Min led the assault in person; they fought at Cangting; Hedou and the others were utterly defeated; twenty-eight thousand dead; pursuing, they beheaded Jin Tun at Yin'an, took all their forces captive, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Min met them at Cangting in person. Hedou's coalition was destroyed—twenty-eight thousand dead. Min pursued, killed Jin Tun at Yin'an, and took every survivor captive.

sentences.zh: 閔戎卒三十餘萬，旌旗、鉦鼓綿亘百餘里，雖石氏之盛，無以過也。

translations.literal: Min's soldiers on campaign numbered more than three hundred thousand; banners, bells, and drums stretched continuously for more than a hundred li—even the height of the Shi clan could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Min now fielded three hundred thousand men; banners and drums stretched a hundred li—surpassing even Shi Hu at his zenith.

sentences.zh: 故晋散騎常侍隴西辛謐，有高名，歷劉、石之世，徵辟皆不就；

translations.literal: Former Jin Regular Cavalier Attendant Xin Mi of Longxi had a lofty reputation; through the Liu and Shi eras, every summons and appointment he declined;
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi of Longxi, former Jin regular cavalier attendant, enjoyed great fame and had refused every office under Liu and Shi;

sentences.zh: 閔備禮徵爲太常。

translations.literal: Min prepared full ceremony to summon him as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Min summoned him with full honors as grand minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 謐遺閔書，以爲：「物極則反，致至則危。

translations.literal: Mi sent Min a letter, holding that "when things reach their extreme they reverse; when favor reaches its peak, danger comes.
translations.idiomatic: “Mi wrote Min that when things reach extremes they reverse, and when power peaks danger follows.

sentences.zh: 君王功已成矣，宜因茲大捷，歸身晋朝，必有由、夷之廉，享松、喬之壽矣。」

translations.literal: Your lordship's merit is already accomplished; you should take advantage of this great victory to return your person to the Jin court—you will surely have the integrity of You and Yi, and enjoy the longevity of Song and Qiao."
translations.idiomatic: Your triumph is complete. Turn now to Jin while victory is fresh—you may yet win the integrity of Boyi and Shuqi and the long life of the immortals."

sentences.zh: 因不食而卒。

translations.literal: He then refused food and died.
translations.idiomatic: He starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 九月，燕王俊南徇冀州，取章武、河間。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yan's Jun drove south through Ji Province, taking Zhangwu and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Murong Jun swept south through Ji, taking Zhangwu and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 初，勃海賈堅，少尚氣節，仕趙爲殿中督。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jia Jian of Bohai in his youth prized spirited integrity and served Zhao as Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jian of Bohai had been a spirited youth who served Zhao as palace director.

sentences.zh: 趙亡，堅弃魏主閔還鄉里，擁部曲數千家。

translations.literal: When Zhao perished, Jian abandoned Wei ruler Min, returned to his native place, and gathered several thousand followers of his household troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao fell he abandoned Min, went home, and raised several thousand retainers.

sentences.zh: 燕慕容評徇勃海，遣使招之，堅終不降。

translations.literal: Yan's Murong Ping drove through Bohai and sent envoys to summon him; Jian would never submit.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping of Yan marched through Bohai and summoned him; Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 評與戰，擒之。

translations.literal: Ping fought him and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping fought and took him.

sentences.zh: 俊以評爲章武太守，封裕爲河間太守。

translations.literal: Jun made Ping Administrator of Zhangwu and Feng Yu Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Ping governor of Zhangwu and Feng Yu governor of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 俊與慕容恪皆愛賈堅之材。

translations.literal: Both Jun and Murong Ke admired Jia Jian's talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Murong Ke both prized Jia Jian's talent.

sentences.zh: 堅時年六十餘，恪聞其善射，置牛百步上以試之。

translations.literal: Jian was then more than sixty years old; Ke, hearing he was skilled at archery, placed an ox a hundred paces away to test him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was past sixty. Hearing of his archery, Ke set an ox a hundred paces off to test him.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「少之時能令不中，今老矣，往往中之。」

translations.literal: Jian said, "In youth I could make shots miss; now in old age, shots often hit."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "In youth I could miss at will. Old age—I mostly hit.

sentences.zh: 乃射再發，一矢拂脊，一矢磨腹，皆附膚落毛，上下如一，觀者咸服其妙。

translations.literal: He shot twice; one arrow grazed the back, one the belly—both only brushed the hide and knocked off hair, upper and lower alike; all who watched admired the finesse.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed twice—one arrow grazing the spine, one the belly, each shaving hide and knocking free a tuft of hair with identical precision. The watchers marveled.

sentences.zh: 俊以堅爲樂陵太守，治高城。

translations.literal: Jun made Jian Administrator of Leling, administering Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Jian governor of Leling from Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 苻菁與張先戰于渭北，擒之，三輔郡縣堡壁皆降。

translations.literal: Fu Jing fought Zhang Xian north of the Wei, captured him, and every stronghold of the three auxiliaries submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jing defeated and captured Xian north of the Wei; every fortress of the three metropolitan districts surrendered.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，苻健長驅至長安，杜洪、張琚奔司竹。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Fu Jian drove swiftly to Chang'an; Du Hong and Zhang Ju fled to Sizhu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Fu Jian raced to Chang'an. Du Hong and Zhang Ju fled to Sizhu.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊還薊，留諸將守之；

translations.literal: Yan's Jun returned to Ji, leaving generals to hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun withdrew to Ji, leaving garrisons behind;

sentences.zh: 俊還龍城，謁陵廟。

translations.literal: Jun returned to Longcheng and paid respects at the royal tombs.
translations.idiomatic: then marched to Longcheng to honor the ancestral shrines.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏主閔帥騎十萬攻襄國。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wei ruler Min led one hundred thousand cavalry to attack Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Min led a hundred thousand horse against Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 署其子太原王胤爲大單于、驃騎大將軍，以降胡一千配之爲麾下。

translations.literal: He appointed his son Prince of Taiyuan Yin Grand Chanyu and Rapid Cavalry Grand General, assigning one thousand surrendered barbarians to him as personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Yin, prince of Taiyuan, grand chanyu and rapid cavalry grand general, with a thousand surrendered barbarians as his guard.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫韋謏諫曰：「胡、羯皆我之仇敵，今來歸附，苟存性命耳；

translations.literal: Minister of the Household Wei Xu remonstrated, saying, "The Hu and Jie are all our deadly foes; those who come to submit now do so only to preserve their lives;
translations.idiomatic: Household minister Wei Xu warned: "Hu and Jie are our mortal enemies. They submit only to survive;

sentences.zh: 萬一爲變，悔之何及！

translations.literal: if they should ever turn, what regret would suffice!
translations.idiomatic: if they rebel, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 請誅屏降胡，去單于之號，以防微杜漸。」

translations.literal: Please execute and expel the surrendered barbarians and remove the title of Chanyu, to nip the evil in the bud."
translations.idiomatic: Execute the surrendered barbarians and abolish the chanyu title before trouble starts."

sentences.zh: 閔方欲撫納群胡，大怒，誅謏及其子伯陽。

translations.literal: Min was just then intending to win over all the barbarians and was greatly enraged; he executed Xu and his son Boyang.
translations.idiomatic: Min, bent on winning the barbarians over, flew into a rage and killed Xu and his son Boyang.

sentences.zh: 甲午，苻健入長安，以民心思晋，乃遣參軍杜山伯詣建康獻捷，幷修好于桓溫。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, Fu Jian entered Chang'an; because the people's hearts inclined toward Jin, he sent Staff Officer Du Shanbo to Jiankang to present a victory report and also seek good relations with Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Fu Jian entered Chang'an. Reading the people's hearts as loyal to Jin, he sent Du Shanbo to Jiankang with news of victory and an overture to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 于是秦、雍夷夏皆附之。

translations.literal: Thereupon both barbarians and Chinese of Qin and Yong submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then every tribe and town of Qin and Yong joined him.

sentences.zh: 趙凉州刺史石寧獨據上邽不下，十二月，苻雄擊斬之。

translations.literal: Zhao's Inspector of Liangzhou Shi Ning alone held Shanggui and would not submit; in the twelfth month Fu Xiong attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao's Liangzhou inspector Shi Ning held Shanggui. In the twelfth month Fu Xiong attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 蔡謨除司徒，三年不就職；

translations.literal: Cai Mo was appointed Secretary of State but for three years did not take office;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo was appointed secretary of state but refused the office for three years;

sentences.zh: 詔書屢下，太后遣使諭意，謨終不受。

translations.literal: imperial edicts went out repeatedly; the Empress Dowager sent envoys to convey her intent, yet Mo never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: edicts piled up and the empress dowager sent envoys, but Mo still refused.

sentences.zh: 于是帝臨軒，遣侍中紀據、黃門郎丁纂徵謨；

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor came to the front hall and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Ju and Yellow Gate Attendant Ding Zuan to summon Mo;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court and dispatched Ji Ju and Ding Zuan to summon Mo;

sentences.zh: 謨陳疾篤，使主簿謝攸陳讓。

translations.literal: Mo claimed grave illness and had his chief clerk Xie You present his declination.
translations.idiomatic: Mo pleaded grave illness and sent his chief clerk Xie You to decline.

sentences.zh: 自旦至申，使者十餘返，而謨不至。

translations.literal: from dawn to mid-afternoon more than ten messengers went back and forth, yet Mo still did not come.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn to midafternoon a dozen envoys shuttled back and forth; Mo never appeared.

sentences.zh: 時帝方八歲，甚倦，問左右曰：「所召人何以至今不來？

translations.literal: The emperor was then only eight years old and very weary; he asked those beside him, "Why has the man summoned not yet come?
translations.idiomatic: The eight-year-old emperor wearied and asked his attendants, "Why has the man we summoned not come?

sentences.zh: 臨軒何時當竟？」

translations.literal: When will this session at the front hall end?"
translations.idiomatic: When will this session end?"

sentences.zh: 太后以君臣俱疲，乃詔：「必不來者，宜罷朝。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, seeing ruler and ministers both exhausted, then issued an edict: "If he will certainly not come, the court session should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing ruler and ministers exhausted, the empress dowager issued an edict: "If he will not come, dismiss court.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍殷浩奏免吏部尚書江虨官。

translations.literal: Army General Yin Hao memorialized to dismiss Jiang Pi from office as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Army general Yin Hao memorialized to dismiss Jiang Pi as director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱令曹曰：「蔡公傲違上命，無人臣之禮。

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Yu directed the ministry, saying, "Lord Cai has defied the supreme command with the arrogance of no subject's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Kuaiji told the ministry: "Lord Cai has defied the throne—no subject's courtesy remains.

sentences.zh: 若人主卑屈于上，大義不行于下，亦不知所以爲政矣。」

translations.literal: If the sovereign humbles himself above while great principle does not prevail below, one also does not know how to govern."
translations.idiomatic: If the throne humbles itself while law dies below, government itself is impossible."

sentences.zh: 公卿乃奏：「謨悖慢傲上，罪同不臣，請送廷尉以正刑書。」

translations.literal: The high ministers then memorialized: "Mo has been rebellious, arrogant, and disrespectful above—a crime equal to disloyalty; please send him to the Court of Justice to receive the written penalty of the law."
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers memorialized: "Mo's insolence equals treason—send him to the Court of Justice for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 謨懼，帥子弟素服詣闕稽顙，自到廷尉待罪。

translations.literal: Mo was afraid; he led sons and nephews in plain garb to the palace gate to knock forehead to earth, and went himself to the Court of Justice to await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Mo led sons and nephews in white to the palace gate to prostrate himself, then surrendered to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 殷浩欲加謨大辟。

translations.literal: Yin Hao wished to add the death sentence for Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao pressed for execution.

sentences.zh: 會徐州刺史荀羨入朝，浩以問羨，羨曰：「蔡公今日事危，明日必有桓、文之舉。」

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Xuzhou Xun Xian was entering court; Hao asked Xian; Xian said, "Lord Cai's affair is dangerous today; tomorrow there may be a deed like Duke Huan's or Duke Wen's."
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xun Xian of Xuzhou arrived at court. Hao consulted him. Xian said, "Lord Cai is cornered today; tomorrow he may act like Duke Huan or Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 浩乃止。

translations.literal: Hao then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hao desisted.

sentences.zh: 下詔免謨爲庶人。

translations.literal: An edict was issued demoting Mo to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Mo to commoner rank.
